sources.title: TrendForce: Memory 1Q26 price surge — Samsung memory ASP +146%, SK hynix DRAM ASP +mid-60% q/q
sources.claims: Samsung average memory ASP (DRAM+NAND) rose ~146% in 1Q26 versus the 2025 full-year average; SK hynix DRAM ASP +mid-60% q/q and NAND ASP +mid-70% q/q; Samsung mobile memory costs for its DX division rose ~107% versus the prior-year average; mobile memory reached 9.4% of Samsung DX procurement mix in 1Q26.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any assumption that Apple's 39.9% products gross margin (9M FY2026) is durable: component cost inflation is running at triple-digit percentages and Apple names memory as a cost headwind in its Q3 FY2026 10-Q.

sources.title: Ninth Circuit opinion, Epic Games v. Apple, No. 25-2935 (2025-12-11): 27% link-out commission had prohibitive effect
sources.claims: The Ninth Circuit held that Apple's 27% commission on purchases made after a user follows a link out of an app had a prohibitive effect and violated the 2021 injunction, and remanded for the district court to decide what commission, if any, Apple may charge on such purchases.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the assumption that App Store take rates (15-30% in-app, 27% link-out) are intact: the link-out commission is unenforceable pending remand, so developers of large digital-goods apps can move payments outside the 15-30% structure.

sources.title: 9to5Mac: Google defends its Safari deal with Apple in antitrust appeal — 36% of Safari search ad revenue, ~$20bn paid in 2022
sources.claims: Court records in the Google search antitrust case show Apple received 36% of search advertising revenue generated through Safari and that Google paid Apple about $20bn in 2022; Judge Mehta's remedy lets Google keep paying Apple for Safari default placement but bans exclusivity and caps any default arrangement at 12 months, giving rivals an annual shot at the placement; Google appealed to the D.C. Circuit on 2026-05-22 seeking reversal in full; Eddy Cue testified Microsoft offered 100% of search ad revenue and Apple still judged Bing less profitable.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that the Google payment is a stable annuity: the 12-month default limit converts a multi-year exclusive into an annually re-bid contract, so the ~$20bn (2022) stream is repriced by negotiation and by rivals' willingness to bid.

sources.title: S&P Global Market Intelligence: Apple earnings preview Q4 2026 — consensus iPhone $56.4bn quarter, $252.4bn FY2026, $277.4bn FY2027
sources.claims: Consensus expects Apple's September 2026 quarter to deliver $56.4bn of iPhone revenue, $252.4bn for fiscal 2026 and $277.4bn for fiscal 2027; the preview flags supply-chain questions and whether Apple can meet upgrade demand plus the Duo foldable in the March 2027 quarter.
sources.claims_weakened: Sets the bar the 2026-11-02 print must clear: consensus iPhone growth of ~20% for FY2026 leaves little room if memory supply constrains the December quarter. Page body returned HTTP 403; figures taken from the indexed summary.

sources.title: MacRumors: Apple to report Q4 FY2026 on November 2, 2026 — guidance +9-11% revenue, iPhone mid-teens
sources.claims: Apple's fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results will be published on 2026-11-02 (call 2:00 p.m. PT) with new CEO John Ternus and CFO Kevan Parekh; on the Q3 FY2026 call CFO Parekh guided September-quarter total revenue to grow 9-11% y/y and iPhone revenue to grow mid-teens with FX headwinds and supply constraints; Q4 FY2025 revenue was $102.5bn, implying $111.7-113.7bn; iPhone Duo foldable launches 2026-10-23 and falls in Q1 FY2027; iPhone 18 Pro launched 2026-09-18; Apple Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 and AirPods 5 shipped in the quarter.
sources.claims_weakened: Establishes that no audited FY2026 full-year statements exist as of 2026-10-31, so any FY2026 annual figure is a nine-month or trailing-twelve-month construction.

sources.title: MacRumors: Apple reaches 2.5 billion active devices (Q1 FY2026, 2026-01-29)
sources.claims: Apple said its installed base passed 2.5 billion active devices in the quarter ended December 2025 (Q1 FY2026), with the increase reported at about 150 million devices since 2025.
sources.claims_weakened: The 2.5 billion figure is a company statement made on an earnings call, not a filed disclosure; Apple's 10-K and 10-Q do not quantify the installed base, so per-device metrics built on it are estimates.

sources.title: Seeking Alpha: Apple Q4 2026 earnings preview — FY2026 iPhone units estimated at 261 million
sources.claims: FY2026 iPhone unit estimates were revised up to 261 million from 258 million since the previous quarter; Apple stock rose 18.4% since May 2026 and 27.5% year to date.
sources.claims_weakened: Unit estimates are third-party and paywalled; Apple has not disclosed iPhone unit sales since FY2019, so any per-unit economics rest on sell-side estimates.

sources.title: Samsung Electronics third quarter 2026 results (KRW 195.3tn revenue, KRW 107.4tn operating profit)
sources.claims: Q3 2026 revenue KRW 195.3tn (+14% q/q) and operating profit KRW 107.4tn; DS (semiconductor) division revenue KRW 147.1tn and operating profit KRW 106.5tn; DX (devices/mobile) division posted an operating loss of KRW 0.8tn; memory prices rose across all applications on server demand; memory business expects 2027 AI-driven demand to exceed industry supply and Q4 2026 demand growth to continue.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that the memory cost cycle peaks in 2026: the supplier expects 2027 demand above supply, so Apple's handset bill of materials keeps rising into FY2027 and its device gross-margin guidance must absorb it.

sources.title: 9to5Mac — Apple's search deal with Google could face renewed scrutiny as DOJ appeals antitrust ruling
sources.claims: Judge Mehta's final judgment of 2025-12-05 preserved Google's ability to pay Apple for non-exclusive default placement, capped default deals at 12 months and barred exclusivity; the DOJ and states cross-appealed in February 2026, so a payment ban remains possible on appeal.
sources.claims_weakened: The remedy did not ban payments, contrary to some secondary reports claiming a 2026 default-payment ban took effect.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom — Apple announces changes for apps in the European Union
sources.claims: From 2026-10-01 Apple's unified EU terms set 26% commission on App Store in-app purchase, 20% on alternative payment processing, 15% on link-outs, and a 5% Core Technology Commission for apps distributed via alternative marketplaces or the web; Apple says the changes resolve disagreements with the Commission.
sources.claims_weakened: Developer groups called the terms unacceptable, so the EU settlement may not be durable; Apple's EU App Store revenue is not disclosed to size the impact.

sources.title: European Commission — Commission finds Apple and Meta in breach of the Digital Markets Act (IP/25/1085)
sources.claims: European Commission found Apple breached the DMA anti-steering obligation and fined it EUR 500 million on 2025-04-23; Meta fined EUR 200 million in the same decision package.
sources.claims_weakened: The fine equals about 0.1% of Apple's FY2025 net sales, so the business-model remedies matter more than the penalty.

sources.title: Cravath — Epic Games' Ninth Circuit win affirming civil contempt finding
sources.claims: Ninth Circuit affirmed the civil contempt finding against Apple on 2025-12-11 for willful violation of the anti-steering injunction; it held Apple may charge only limited fees on linked transactions tied to the cost of services it provides, and affirmed the steering injunction.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple's ability to charge any commission on external purchases in the US is now constrained, reducing App Store take-rate control independent of the DOJ case.

sources.title: Stratrix — Why Google pays Apple $20 billion a year for default search
sources.claims: Google paid Apple about $20 billion in 2022 for Safari default search placement, equal to 36% of Google's Safari search revenue, per the US v. Google trial record; Judge Mehta's 2024 liability ruling made the payments central evidence.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple does not disclose the payment, so the current amount and margin are unverified; the 2022 trial figure may overstate or understate today's run rate.

sources.title: U.S. and Plaintiff States v. Apple Inc. — DOJ Antitrust Division case page
sources.claims: DOJ and 16 states/DC filed a civil monopolization case against Apple on 2024-03-21 in the District of New Jersey; DOJ seeks equitable relief, not damages.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple's 10-K says it has substantial defenses; no ruling on the merits has been issued.

sources.title: Ashurst — EU General Court rejects Apple challenges to European Commission DMA designation decisions
sources.claims: On 2026-07-08 the EU General Court dismissed Apple's challenges to its DMA gatekeeper designation for the App Store, iOS and Safari; the substance of Apple's Article 6(7) interoperability challenge is unresolved and a first-instance ruling is unlikely before late 2027, so Apple must comply meanwhile.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple's DMA appeal therefore offers little near-term relief from interoperability obligations.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom: App Store ecosystem reaches record $1.4 trillion
sources.claims: Apple-commissioned study: App Store ecosystem facilitated ~$1.4T of developer billings and sales in 2025, up from ~$1.3T in 2024; physical goods and services ~$1.1T, in-app advertising ~$151B, digital goods and services ~$149B; 850M average weekly visitors across 175 countries. Company-provided and not independently audited.
sources.claims_weakened: The $1.4T figure measures gross ecosystem commerce, not Apple revenue; only the ~$149B digital-goods slice is commissionable, so it overstates the services revenue pool if read as TAM.

sources.title: IDC: Smartphone Shipments Set for Record 16.7% Drop in 2026, as the Memory Crisis Hits Full Force
sources.claims: 2026 global smartphone shipments -16.7% to just over 1.0B units, steepest annual contraction on record; total market value +6.3% to $613B; ASP $581 (+27.6%); NAND/DRAM costs up >300% YoY; Android -24.3%, share down 7pp; iOS shipments -1.3%, share up ~4pp to record 23.6%; HarmonyOS nearly triples to 51M units; Apple foldable entry H2 2026, >17M foldable iPhones by 2027, ~40% of foldables, ASP >$2,550, >$45.7B value; memory supply stabilises 2028.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any assumption of unit-led market growth to 2030: the market is shrinking in units while growing in value, and Apple's near-term growth depends on price/mix and a new foldable category, not market volume.

sources.title: IDC Worldwide Wearable Device Tracker: Q2 2026 results and 2026-2030 forecast
sources.claims: Wearable shipments ~148M units in Q2 2026, +2.7% YoY; Apple 15.5% share (+8.9%), Xiaomi 11.7% (-6.6%), Huawei 10.9% (+8.4%), Samsung 6.8% (-2.9%). Apple leads earwear with 17.2%; Huawei leads smartwatches 18.8% vs Apple 17.2%. 2026 forecast ~625M units (+1.7%), 2.4% CAGR 2026-2030 to ~687M units; smartwatches -3.7% in 2026; glasses +35.2% in 2026, 18.1% CAGR.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens a wearables recovery story: smartwatches shrink in 2026 and Apple's overall wearables share (15.5%) is below its 2025 peak quarters (21.0% in Q4 2025).

sources.title: Huawei 2025 Annual Report press release
sources.claims: Huawei 2025 revenue CNY880.9B, net profit CNY68B, R&D CNY192.3B (21.8% of revenue), audited by KPMG; consumer business "worked to overcome formidable challenges" and drove the HarmonyOS ecosystem; closing rate USD1 = CNY6.9906.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that US export controls have neutralised Huawei as a premium competitor: it still funds R&D at ~22% of revenue and grew smartphone share in China in 2026.

sources.title: IDC: Why Huawei and Apple Grew While China's Smartphone Market Fell Again in Q2 2026
sources.claims: China smartphone shipments ~66M units in Q2 2026, -4.3% YoY, fifth straight decline; H1 2026 ~134M units, -4.2%. Vendor shares Q2 2026: Huawei 22.6% (+19.4% YoY), Apple 18.1% (+24.4%), OPPO 16.0%, vivo 16.0%, Xiaomi 12.4% (-21.7%), Honor 11.3%. Top six ~96% of market. IDC expects China decline to widen to ~20% in H2 2026 and recovery around 2028-2029. Apple and Huawei held prices while Android vendors raised them; Apple's signalling of H2 price increases pulled demand forward.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that Apple's China revenue growth (+30% 9M FY2026) is a durable share recovery: it coincides with a shrinking market, price-increase pull-forward and Huawei at a five-year share high.

sources.title: TWICE reporting Omdia: average smartphone price to reach $565 in 2026
sources.claims: Omdia: global smartphone ASP forecast to rise from $467 in 2025 to $565 in 2026, +21% (+$98), the largest annual increase on record; DRAM and NAND prices up more than 80% in Q1 2026; vendors prioritising value over volume.

sources.title: The Desk reporting WARC: global ad spending forecast $1.34 trillion in 2026
sources.claims: WARC Media: global advertising spend forecast to grow 11.9% to $1.34T in 2026, after 10% growth in both 2024 and 2025; social media advertising +21.3% to $394.6B; VOD/streaming ad spending +15.1%.

sources.title: China Biz Insider: Xiaomi Q2 2026 results, memory squeezes phones
sources.claims: Xiaomi Q2 2026: group revenue RMB108.9B; smartphone shipments 31.2M units, 11.5% global share; smartphone gross margin 8.5% as memory costs rose 78-83%; adjusted net profit -42.6% YoY.

sources.title: FoneArena reporting Samsung Q3 2026 results: mobile loss despite revenue growth
sources.claims: Samsung Electronics Q3 2026: MX and Networks revenue KRW37.7T (+10.55% YoY, +13.55% QoQ), operating loss KRW0.6T, second consecutive quarterly loss despite 11% higher smartphone revenue; group profit driven by record memory earnings; flagship and foldable launches supported mobile revenue.

sources.title: Counterpoint Research: Global smartphone shipments grew 2% YoY in 2025
sources.claims: Counterpoint Research: global smartphone shipments grew 2% YoY in 2025; Apple led with 20% share and 10% YoY growth, the highest among the top five; Samsung grew 5% with 19% share; Xiaomi third but Q4 2025 shipments -11% YoY. Methodology: Market Monitor OEM shipment by region, published August 2026.

sources.title: 9to5Mac: Spotify crosses 300 million paid subscribers as Apple Music readies iOS 27
sources.claims: Spotify crossed 300 million paying subscribers (August 2026), after 293M Premium subscribers and 761M MAU at Q1 2026 (Spotify disclosure, 2026-04-28); Apple Music estimated at ~100-108M subscribers by MIDiA and other analysts.

sources.title: AppleInsider reporting Counterpoint: Apple holds 65% of premium smartphone market, H1 2026
sources.claims: Counterpoint Research Handset Model Sales Tracker (wholesale ASP >= $600): premium segment unit sales +5% YoY in H1 2026; premium share of global smartphone sales 29% in H1 2026 vs 25% H1 2025 and 20% H1 2022 (record); Apple 65% of global premium unit sales in H1 2026, +9% YoY, driven by iPhone 17 lineup.

sources.title: 9to5Mac reporting IDC: Apple grows Mac shipments as broader PC market declines (Q2 2026)
sources.claims: IDC PC Tracker Q2 2026: global PC shipments 68.2M units, -4.9% YoY, first decline since 2024; Lenovo 24.4% share, HP 19.1%, Dell 13.6%, Apple 9.9% (+10.1% shipments, only major vendor with significant growth, helped by MacBook Neo launch), ASUS 7.4%. IDC: units falling while revenue climbs because vendors push price increases faster than demand falls; no inventory pull-forward expected in H2 2026; memory shortage not easing until early 2028.

sources.title: Counterpoint via TelecomLead: China smartphone shipments -10% YoY in Q3 2026; Huawei 21.3% share, Apple 19.5% (+4.8pp); iPhone 18 Pro launch sales +23.5%
sources.claims: China smartphone market contracted 10% YoY in Q3 2026 (Counterpoint); Huawei 21.3% shipment share vs Apple 19.5%, Apple up 4.8pp from 14.7%; iPhone 18 Pro first-three-week sales +23.5% vs iPhone 17 Pro launch; standard iPhone 18 launch moved to 2027; Omdia estimates market -12% to 59.3m units with Apple 11.6m.
sources.claims_weakened: The framing that Apple is losing China share to Huawei; the assumption that iPhone volume growth is broad-based rather than Pro-mix driven.

sources.title: FinanceCharts: Apple P/E 39.52x trailing and 35.21x forward as of 2026-10-30, 12-month average 35.66x
sources.claims: AAPL trailing P/E 39.52x and forward P/E 35.21x at the 2026-10-30 close; trailing P/E 10.82% above its 12-month average of 35.66x.
sources.claims_weakened: Any claim that the multiple is at or below its own recent average, or that valuation offers a margin of safety.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom: Tim Cook to become Executive Chairman, John Ternus CEO effective 2026-09-01
sources.claims: Board unanimously approved Tim Cook moving to executive chairman and John Ternus, SVP Hardware Engineering, becoming CEO effective 2026-09-01.
sources.claims_weakened: Continuity assumptions: the first earnings call under a new CEO is 2026-11-02, with margin and AI strategy questions open.

sources.title: TrendForce: iPhone 18 Pro 256GB BOM cost +38% YoY, memory ~34% of BOM in 3Q26 vs ~10% a year earlier
sources.claims: 512GB-class iPhone 18 Pro 256GB bill of materials up ~38% YoY; memory share of BOM rose from ~10% to ~34% in 3Q26 and expected above 40% in 1H27; memory prices up five- to sevenfold since start-2025; Apple likely to sacrifice gross margin to limit price increases; global smartphone production under pressure 2H26-2027.
sources.claims_weakened: The assumption that Apple can hold ~47-48% gross margin through the iPhone 18 cycle; the view that component cost inflation is a one-quarter issue.

sources.title: CRS Legal Sidebar LSB11362: Federal court endorses behavioral remedies, rejects structural relief in Google search case
sources.claims: Congressional Research Service analysis of the Google search remedies ruling: the court endorsed behavioural remedies and rejected structural relief; under a broad payment ban, distribution partners would face a choice between placing Google Search as default without payment or entering less lucrative deals.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that the judgment broke up Google or banned all default-search payments.

sources.title: Hughes Hubbard: Court issues remedies ruling in United States v. Google Search case — exclusivity barred, payments not banned
sources.claims: In the September 2025 remedies ruling in United States v. Google, the court did not ban Google's payments to distribution partners such as Apple for default search placement; it prohibited exclusive search distribution agreements, required sharing of search index and syndication data at marginal cost, and declined structural relief.
sources.claims_weakened: Secondary commentary claiming the remedy banned Google's ~$20bn annual payments to Apple, or that it imposed search choice screens.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Apple overhauls its EU App Store fees, loosens rules for alternative app stores
sources.claims: Apple overhauled EU App Store fees in August 2026 to resolve its DMA dispute: it had been fined EUR500 million for non-compliance in 2025 and faced further penalties; the new terms replace the Core Technology Fee with a 5% Core Technology Commission and set commission rates for alternative payments and link-outs.

rows.finding: The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500 million on 2025-04-23 for breaching the DMA anti-steering obligation; Apple's revised EU terms effective 2026-10-01 cut in-app-purchase commission to 26% (from 30%), alternative payment to 20%, link-outs to 15%, and set a 5% Core Technology Commission for apps distributed via alternative marketplaces or the web.
rows.mechanism: The fine is a rounding error; the fee schedule transfers take rate from Apple to developers and lowers the cost of distributing outside the App Store, compressing the highest-margin revenue pool.
rows.benchmark: EUR 500 million is about 0.1% of FY2025 net sales of $416.2 billion; the DMA allows fines up to 10% of worldwide annual turnover.
rows.weakens: Apple says the terms resolve its disagreements with the Commission and keeps a 26% in-app rate; EU developer groups called the terms unacceptable, so the settlement is contested and may not be durable.
rows.implication: Underwrite EU App Store revenue at a lower take rate: each $1 billion of annual commission lost equals roughly $0.75 billion of gross profit at the 75.4% Services gross margin.
rows.confidence: high on the terms, low on revenue sizing because Apple does not disclose EU App Store revenue
rows.follow_up: What is Apple's EU App Store billings and commission revenue, and will the Commission formally close the Article 6(4) proceeding?

rows.finding: Google paid Apple about $20 billion in 2022 for Safari default placement, equal to 36% of Google's Safari search revenue per the US v. Google trial record; Apple does not disclose the payment. At $20 billion, the payment equals 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue of $109.2 billion and about 15% of FY2025 operating income if treated as near-pure margin.
rows.mechanism: Default placement is rent on the OS choke point; a payment ban or lower revenue share removes high-margin revenue without removing much cost, hitting operating income almost dollar for dollar.
rows.benchmark: Judge Mehta's final judgment of 2025-12-05 preserved non-exclusive payments, capped default deals at 12 months and banned exclusivity; the DOJ and states cross-appealed in February 2026 seeking a payment ban.
rows.weakens: Payments survived the remedy; Apple can re-bid annually and may replace some search revenue with AI subscription deals; the $20 billion figure is from 2022, not a current disclosure.
rows.implication: Price a 10-15% operating-income tail with an appellate decision likely in 2027; a negotiated lower rate is more likely than zero, but either outcome compresses Services growth and multiple.
rows.confidence: medium: the 2022 figure is from the trial record, the current amount is undisclosed
rows.follow_up: What is the current annual payment and contract term, and when will the D.C. Circuit rule on the payment-ban appeal?

rows.finding: The DOJ and 16 states and the District of Columbia sued Apple on 2024-03-21 alleging monopolization or attempted monopolization in 'performance smartphones' and 'smartphones'; the DOJ seeks equitable relief only, and the case remains pending in the District of New Jersey with no trial date disclosed in Apple's 2026 filings.
rows.mechanism: An equitable remedy can force interoperability or App Store rule changes; the cost is business-model change rather than a damages cheque.
rows.benchmark: Apple's own risk factor states adverse antitrust outcomes can require further business changes and significant fines; no monetary claim has been disclosed.
rows.weakens: Apple says it has substantial defenses and intends to defend vigorously; the motion-to-dismiss outcome and docket are not visible in Apple's filings.
rows.implication: Treat this as a long-dated tail and model remedy scenarios (external purchase links, messaging and wallet access) rather than a settlement payment.
rows.confidence: medium-high: filing facts are clear, the litigation path is not
rows.follow_up: What is the trial schedule and which remedy theories survived Apple's motion to dismiss?

rows.finding: The Ninth Circuit on 2025-12-11 affirmed the civil contempt finding against Apple for willfully violating the anti-steering injunction and held Apple may charge only limited fees on linked transactions tied to the cost of services it provides; the Supreme Court granted certiorari on 2026-06-30.
rows.mechanism: US App Store commission on external purchases is being narrowed by the courts independently of the DOJ case, reducing Apple's take-rate control.
rows.benchmark: Before 2024 Apple banned steering entirely; the injunction now requires links and limits fees to a cost-justified level.
rows.weakens: The Supreme Court could reverse or narrow the contempt ruling by mid-2027, and Apple still controls in-app purchase.
rows.implication: Assume continued pressure on US external-purchase commission revenue and require any fee regime to be cost-justified.
rows.confidence: high on the Ninth Circuit ruling, medium on the final outcome
rows.follow_up: What issues did the Supreme Court agree to review, and what is the argument and decision timing?

rows.finding: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $109.4 billion with gross margin of 50.1%, including about 2 percentage points from tariff refunds; EPS of $2.02 included $0.11 from refunds. FY2025 products gross margin fell on tariff costs.
rows.mechanism: Refunds from struck-down IEEPA tariffs flatter the current margin; underlying gross margin is about 48%, and Section 232 or Section 301 actions could re-impose cost.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 total gross margin was 46.9%; Q3 FY2026 underlying gross margin is about 48.1% after removing the roughly 2-point refund benefit.
rows.weakens: The Section 232 semiconductor initial results of 2026-01-14 imposed no additional tariffs on Apple products, and the refunds are cash-positive.
rows.implication: Do not capitalise the refund; underwrite a 47-48% gross margin with tariff tail risk rather than the reported 50%.
rows.confidence: high: figures are from Apple's earnings release and 10-Q
rows.follow_up: How much refund remains, and what Section 301 rate applies to China-assembled iPhones?

rows.finding: The board has eight directors, three of them women (37.5%), with an independent chair separate from the CEO; the Audit Committee oversees privacy and cybersecurity; Say-on-Pay support was 92% in 2025; the related-party threshold is $120,000; Apple employed about 166,000 full-time-equivalent staff at 2025-09-27.
rows.mechanism: Governance quality lowers the tail risk of self-dealing and oversight failure; ESG controversies matter only where they change demand, costs or legal exposure.
rows.benchmark: Apple has no dual-class shares and an independent chair; its 37.5% female board is at or above the large-cap norm, but the chair has served since 2000 and the board is ageing.
rows.weakens: The 10-K admits supplier code violations occur from time to time, and Apple's climate and labour metrics are company-reported and were not independently verified in this run.
rows.implication: No governance discount is warranted; the material ESG gaps are supply-chain labour disclosure and compliance culture after the contempt finding.
rows.confidence: high on board composition, low on ESG performance
rows.follow_up: What are the latest supplier audit findings on child and forced labour, and what is the board retirement policy?

rows.finding: The EU Court of Justice confirmed the Commission's 2016 State Aid decision on 2024-09-10; Apple recorded a $10.2 billion net one-time tax charge and paid $15.8 billion to Ireland from escrow.
rows.mechanism: A realised tax tail rather than a recurring cost; it explains the FY2024 effective-tax-rate spike and Apple's non-GAAP adjustment.
rows.benchmark: Q4 FY2024 tax provision was $14.9 billion versus $5.3 billion in Q4 FY2025, and FY2024 GAAP net income was $93.7 billion versus $112.0 billion in FY2025.
rows.weakens: Apple has paid the amount and the case is closed.
rows.implication: No ongoing cash impact, but it demonstrates that EU tax policy can impose multi-billion retroactive charges.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Do Pillar Two or other EU tax proposals raise Apple's ongoing effective tax rate?

plan.decision_question: Which regulatory, policy and ESG issues are material enough to change the investment case for a long-only holder, and what is their dollar or margin impact?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's regulatory exposure, not its ESG record, is the material issue: EU and US platform remedies now target the two purest-margin revenue streams, the roughly $20 billion Google default payment and App Store commissions, so a long-only case must price a 10-15% operating-income tail and a lower Services multiple, while the tariff refund that lifted Q3 FY2026 gross margin by about 2 points is a one-off rather than a new margin level.
plan.why_different: This section prices legal and policy tails and governance quality; it does not re-tell demand, product or valuation, and it treats ESG only where an issue can change cash flow, the cost of capital or the multiple.
plan.mechanism: Platform regulation transfers take rate and default-placement rent from Apple to developers and rivals; fines are small relative to revenue, so remedies and fee schedules rather than penalties drive the dollar impact; tariffs shift product cost between periods; governance affects oversight and legal-risk control.
plan.comparison_set: DMA gatekeeper peers (Google, Meta), the pre-2024 App Store regime, Apple's FY2025 gross margin of 46.9% and Services margin of 75.4%, and the historical base rate that US antitrust appeals rarely produce structural breakup.
plan.counter_evidence: Judge Mehta preserved Google's payments; Apple's August 2026 EU terms concede little on the headline in-app rate; DMA fines are about 0.1% of revenue; the DOJ seeks equitable relief only; tariff refunds are a cash tailwind; and Apple's brand has absorbed labour and privacy controversies without visible demand damage.
plan.visual: Policy impact matrix with exposure, probability and dollar or margin impact, plus the regulatory record table.
plan.prohibited: ESG is strong; risks are manageable; well positioned; committed to sustainability without evidence; vague counts such as many investigations; treating the $20 billion as an Apple disclosure.

rows.finding: The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500 million on 2025-04-23 for breaching the DMA anti-steering obligation; Apple's revised EU terms effective 2026-10-01 cut in-app-purchase commission to 26% (from 30%), alternative payment to 20%, link-outs to 15%, and set a 5% Core Technology Commission for apps distributed via alternative marketplaces or the web.
rows.mechanism: The fine is a rounding error; the fee schedule transfers take rate from Apple to developers and lowers the cost of distributing outside the App Store, compressing the highest-margin revenue pool.
rows.benchmark: EUR 500 million is about 0.1% of FY2025 net sales of $416.2 billion; the DMA allows fines up to 10% of worldwide annual turnover.
rows.weakens: Apple says the terms resolve its disagreements with the Commission and keeps a 26% in-app rate; EU developer groups called the terms unacceptable, so the settlement is contested and may not be durable.
rows.implication: Underwrite EU App Store revenue at a lower take rate: each $1 billion of annual commission lost equals roughly $0.75 billion of gross profit at the 75.4% Services gross margin.
rows.confidence: high on the terms, low on revenue sizing because Apple does not disclose EU App Store revenue
rows.follow_up: What is Apple's EU App Store billings and commission revenue, and will the Commission formally close the Article 6(4) proceeding?

rows.finding: Google paid Apple about $20 billion in 2022 for Safari default placement, equal to 36% of Google's Safari search revenue per the US v. Google trial record; Apple does not disclose the payment. At $20 billion, the payment equals 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue of $109.2 billion and about 15% of FY2025 operating income if treated as near-pure margin.
rows.mechanism: Default placement is rent on the OS choke point; a payment ban or lower revenue share removes high-margin revenue without removing much cost, hitting operating income almost dollar for dollar.
rows.benchmark: Judge Mehta's final judgment of 2025-12-05 preserved non-exclusive payments, capped default deals at 12 months and banned exclusivity; the DOJ and states cross-appealed in February 2026 seeking a payment ban.
rows.weakens: Payments survived the remedy; Apple can re-bid annually and may replace some search revenue with AI subscription deals; the $20 billion figure is from 2022, not a current disclosure.
rows.implication: Price a 10-15% operating-income tail with an appellate decision likely in 2027; a negotiated lower rate is more likely than zero, but either outcome compresses Services growth and multiple.
rows.confidence: medium: the 2022 figure is from the trial record, the current amount is undisclosed
rows.follow_up: What is the current annual payment and contract term, and when will the D.C. Circuit rule on the payment-ban appeal?

rows.finding: The DOJ and 16 states and the District of Columbia sued Apple on 2024-03-21 alleging monopolization or attempted monopolization in 'performance smartphones' and 'smartphones'; the DOJ seeks equitable relief only, and the case remains pending in the District of New Jersey with no trial date disclosed in Apple's 2026 filings.
rows.mechanism: An equitable remedy can force interoperability or App Store rule changes; the cost is business-model change rather than a damages cheque.
rows.benchmark: Apple's own risk factor states adverse antitrust outcomes can require further business changes and significant fines; no monetary claim has been disclosed.
rows.weakens: Apple says it has substantial defenses and intends to defend vigorously; the motion-to-dismiss outcome and docket are not visible in Apple's filings.
rows.implication: Treat this as a long-dated tail and model remedy scenarios (external purchase links, messaging and wallet access) rather than a settlement payment.
rows.confidence: medium-high: filing facts are clear, the litigation path is not
rows.follow_up: What is the trial schedule and which remedy theories survived Apple's motion to dismiss?

rows.finding: The Ninth Circuit on 2025-12-11 affirmed the civil contempt finding against Apple for willfully violating the anti-steering injunction and held Apple may charge only limited fees on linked transactions tied to the cost of services it provides; the Supreme Court granted certiorari on 2026-06-30.
rows.mechanism: US App Store commission on external purchases is being narrowed by the courts independently of the DOJ case, reducing Apple's take-rate control.
rows.benchmark: Before 2024 Apple banned steering entirely; the injunction now requires links and limits fees to a cost-justified level.
rows.weakens: The Supreme Court could reverse or narrow the contempt ruling by mid-2027, and Apple still controls in-app purchase.
rows.implication: Assume continued pressure on US external-purchase commission revenue and require any fee regime to be cost-justified.
rows.confidence: high on the Ninth Circuit ruling, medium on the final outcome
rows.follow_up: What issues did the Supreme Court agree to review, and what is the argument and decision timing?

rows.finding: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $109.4 billion with gross margin of 50.1%, including about 2 percentage points from tariff refunds; EPS of $2.02 included $0.11 from refunds. FY2025 products gross margin fell on tariff costs.
rows.mechanism: Refunds from struck-down IEEPA tariffs flatter the current margin; underlying gross margin is about 48%, and Section 232 or Section 301 actions could re-impose cost.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 total gross margin was 46.9%; Q3 FY2026 underlying gross margin is about 48.1% after removing the roughly 2-point refund benefit.
rows.weakens: The Section 232 semiconductor initial results of 2026-01-14 imposed no additional tariffs on Apple products, and the refunds are cash-positive.
rows.implication: Do not capitalise the refund; underwrite a 47-48% gross margin with tariff tail risk rather than the reported 50%.
rows.confidence: high: figures are from Apple's earnings release and 10-Q
rows.follow_up: How much refund remains, and what Section 301 rate applies to China-assembled iPhones?

rows.finding: On 2026-09-01 Tim Cook moved from CEO to Executive Chair, John Ternus became CEO and a ninth director, and Arthur Levinson became Lead Independent Director; the 2026 proxy shows eight directors standing, four of them women (Austin, Jung, Lozano, Wagner), no dual-class stock, a $120,000 related-party threshold, and a board waiver of its age-75 guideline for Levinson (75) and Audit Chair Ron Sugar (77), both re-elected on 2026-02-24; the 2026 advisory executive-pay vote passed. Apple employed about 166,000 full-time-equivalent staff at 2025-09-27.
rows.mechanism: Succession was executed without a dual-class structure, but the board's independence check moves from an independent chair to a lead independent director, and the age waiver slows refreshment, so oversight quality now depends on the lead director and committee chairs rather than the chair.
rows.benchmark: Apple has no dual-class shares; four of eight 2026 nominees were women, or 44% of the nine-person board after Ternus joined; the chair had served since 2000 and the board waived its own retirement age for two members.
rows.weakens: The chair is now the former CEO rather than an independent director, and the 92% Say-on-Pay figure was not reconfirmed for 2026; the 10-K admits supplier code violations occur from time to time, and climate and labour metrics are company-reported.
rows.implication: No governance discount is warranted on disclosure or control, but the independent check is weaker than the 2026 proxy's independent-chair description; the material ESG gaps remain supply-chain labour disclosure and compliance culture after the contempt finding.
rows.confidence: high on structure and dates, low on ESG performance
rows.follow_up: What are the latest supplier audit findings on child and forced labour, and will the board keep the executive-chair structure or name an independent chair?

rows.finding: The EU Court of Justice confirmed the Commission's 2016 State Aid decision on 2024-09-10; Apple recorded a $10.2 billion net one-time tax charge and paid $15.8 billion to Ireland from escrow.
rows.mechanism: A realised tax tail rather than a recurring cost; it explains the FY2024 effective-tax-rate spike and Apple's non-GAAP adjustment.
rows.benchmark: Q4 FY2024 tax provision was $14.9 billion versus $5.3 billion in Q4 FY2025, and FY2024 GAAP net income was $93.7 billion versus $112.0 billion in FY2025.
rows.weakens: Apple has paid the amount and the case is closed.
rows.implication: No ongoing cash impact, but it demonstrates that EU tax policy can impose multi-billion retroactive charges.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Do Pillar Two or other EU tax proposals raise Apple's ongoing effective tax rate?

plan.decision_question: Which regulatory, policy and ESG issues are material enough to change the investment case for a long-only holder, and what is their dollar or margin impact?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's regulatory exposure, not its ESG record, is the material issue: EU and US platform remedies now target the two purest-margin revenue streams, the roughly $20 billion Google default payment and App Store commissions, so a long-only case must price a 10-15% operating-income tail and a lower Services multiple, while the tariff refund that lifted Q3 FY2026 gross margin by about 2 points is a one-off rather than a new margin level.
plan.why_different: This section prices legal and policy tails and governance quality; it does not re-tell demand, product or valuation, and it treats ESG only where an issue can change cash flow, the cost of capital or the multiple.
plan.mechanism: Platform regulation transfers take rate and default-placement rent from Apple to developers and rivals; fines are small relative to revenue, so remedies and fee schedules rather than penalties drive the dollar impact; tariffs shift product cost between periods; governance affects oversight and legal-risk control.
plan.comparison_set: DMA gatekeeper peers (Google, Meta), the pre-2024 App Store regime, Apple's FY2025 gross margin of 46.9% and Services margin of 75.4%, and the historical base rate that US antitrust appeals rarely produce structural breakup.
plan.counter_evidence: Judge Mehta preserved Google's payments; Apple's August 2026 EU terms concede little on the headline in-app rate; DMA fines are about 0.1% of revenue; the DOJ seeks equitable relief only; tariff refunds are a cash tailwind; the chair is now the former CEO though the board remains majority independent; and Apple's brand has absorbed labour and privacy controversies without visible demand damage.
plan.visual: Policy impact matrix with exposure, probability and dollar or margin impact, plus the regulatory record table.
plan.prohibited: ESG is strong; risks are manageable; well positioned; committed to sustainability without evidence; vague counts such as many investigations; treating the $20 billion as an Apple disclosure; describing the chair as independent after 2026-09-01.

rows.finding: Trailing-twelve-month to 2026-06-27 revenue was $466,823M: iPhone $245,540M (52.6%), Services $120,478M (25.8%), Mac $35,863M, Wearables $36,290M, iPad $28,652M. Services is 25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit ($91,607M of $227,123M).
rows.mechanism: A low-frequency, high-ticket hardware transaction installs an annuity: each device creates a multi-year stream of 76%-gross-margin services (App Store, iCloud, advertising, AppleCare) that costs almost nothing incremental to serve.
rows.benchmark: FY2023: Services 22.2% of revenue and 35.7% of gross profit; FY2025: 26.2% and 42.2%.
rows.weakens: Services share of revenue FELL to 25.2% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 from 26.2% in FY2025 because iPhone grew 22.4% and Services 14.1%, so the 2026 acceleration is hardware-led, not annuity-led.
rows.implication: Underwrite the hardware cycle for the next 12 months and the services annuity for the terminal value; do not treat 2026 growth as proof of services compounding.
rows.confidence: high — both figures are filed segment data
rows.follow_up: Does services growth re-accelerate after the Siri AI launch and the iPhone Duo foldable in FY2027, or does the hardware mix keep rising?

rows.finding: Services gross profit of $91,607M on a trailing-twelve-month basis covers total company R&D of $42,901M 2.1 times, and R&D rose 32.5% year over year in the nine months to 2026-06-27 (to $34,035M) mostly on AI infrastructure.
rows.mechanism: Ownership of the silicon, operating system and billing rails turns third-party distribution and advertising demand into a toll: Apple books the margin without carrying the content or the inventory.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft's FY2026 gross margin was 67.9% on $331,839M of revenue; Apple's blended gross margin was 48.7% TTM.
rows.weakens: The toll rests on two contested arrangements: the App Store commission (Ninth Circuit vacated the 27% link-out commission on 2025-12-11) and the Google default-search revenue share (36% of Safari search advertising, about $20bn in 2022, now capped at 12-month terms).
rows.implication: The services annuity is the valuation floor and the regulatory attack on it is the main threat to the multiple, not to near-term revenue.
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic, medium on durability
rows.follow_up: What share of Services gross profit is App Store commission plus search licensing, and what is management's contingency plan if the link-out remand sets the commission at zero?

rows.finding: On the 2.5 billion active devices Apple cited in January 2026, TTM revenue is about $187 per device per year, gross profit $91, SG&A $11.7, R&D $17.2 and operating profit $62 — a selling cost of 6.3% of revenue.
rows.mechanism: The installed base is a pre-paid distribution network: the next service or accessory sold to an existing customer carries no acquisition cost, so contribution margin approaches gross margin.
rows.benchmark: Samsung's device (DX) division posted a KRW 0.8tn operating LOSS in Q3 2026 on the same handset demand, versus Apple's 32.6% operating margin.
rows.weakens: 2.5 billion is an earnings-call statement, not a filed figure, and Apple has not disclosed device counts in its 10-K; a 20% error in the base moves every per-device number by 20%.
rows.implication: Per-device LTV:CAC is not the constraint on the business — price is. The model is worth owning at a hardware-plus-annuity multiple, not at a software multiple.
rows.confidence: medium — the base is company-stated and unverifiable in filings
rows.follow_up: Will Apple resume disclosing the installed base numerically, and what is the paid-subscription count behind the services line?

rows.finding: Cash conversion cycle was -56.8 days TTM (DSO 24.5, DIO 16.9, DPO 98.3) with accounts payable of $64,525M against inventory of $11,092M at 2026-06-27; suppliers and channel finance the cycle.
rows.mechanism: Apple collects from carriers and retailers before it pays assemblers, so growth releases working capital instead of consuming it and the buyback is self-funded.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft -67.5 days and Alphabet +39.2 days TTM; Apple's own FY2024 cycle was -75.8 days.
rows.weakens: The benefit narrowed: payables fell $5,335M and inventory rose $5,374M in the nine months to 2026-06-27, consistent with pre-buying memory ahead of price increases.
rows.implication: Near-zero CAC payback in cash terms is a structural advantage that does not depend on scale economies others could copy quickly.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: How much of the inventory build is strategic memory pre-buy versus unsold iPhone 18 channel stock?

rows.finding: Products gross margin rose to 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 from 36.9% a year earlier, and Q3 FY2026 total gross margin of 50.1% included about 2 percentage points from tariff refunds ($0.11 of the $2.02 EPS); memory ASPs rose about 146% in Q1 2026 versus the 2025 average.
rows.mechanism: Brand pricing power plus a Pro-model mix shift lift revenue per handset, but the cost side is set by a memory oligopoly whose prices are now rising faster than Apple can re-price.
rows.benchmark: Products gross margin was 36.5% in FY2023, 37.2% in FY2024 and 36.8% in FY2025 — a 36-37% band before this year's 39.9%.
rows.weakens: Two of the levers are temporary: tariff refunds are a one-time recovery and the memory cycle is turning against Apple, with Samsung guiding 2027 memory demand above supply.
rows.implication: Do not capitalise the 50% gross margin; a 47-48% normalised margin is the defensible base case and the gap is roughly 5% of TTM EPS.
rows.confidence: high on the facts, medium on the normalised level
rows.follow_up: What gross-margin range did management guide for the December 2026 quarter, and how much memory cost is contracted versus spot?

rows.finding: The Google default-search relationship is disclosed only through litigation: Apple received 36% of search advertising revenue generated through Safari and about $20bn in 2022; the remedy bars exclusivity and caps any default deal at 12 months, and Google appealed on 2026-05-22.
rows.mechanism: Apple rents the default slot on a device it already owns; the rent is pure margin but is now renegotiated annually against rival bidders and against AI answer engines that shrink search query volume.
rows.benchmark: $20bn is about 17% of TTM Services revenue of $120,478M and about 13% of TTM operating income of $154,859M.
rows.weakens: Apple has never disclosed the payment in a filing, so the share of the current $120bn services line that is search rent is unverified; the $20bn is a 2022 court figure.
rows.implication: A halving of the payment costs about 6-7% of EPS and a full loss about 13%; this is the largest single identifiable risk to the services annuity.
rows.confidence: medium — a dated court figure, not a company disclosure
rows.follow_up: Has Apple disclosed any revenue-share terms in its FY2026 10-K risk factors, and what did Microsoft or others bid in the 2026 renegotiation?

rows.finding: Apple's four hardware lines are sold through direct channels for 40% of net sales and indirect for 60%, with iPhone revenue up 22.4% and Greater China up 30% in the nine months to 2026-06-27.
rows.mechanism: Carrier and reseller channels carry inventory and credit risk, which keeps Apple's receivables at 24.5 days while the carrier subsidises the handset at the point of sale.
rows.benchmark: Greater China was the only segment to shrink in FY2025 (-4%) and is now the fastest-growing (+30% in 9M FY2026), a swing of about 34 percentage points.
rows.weakens: China growth of 30% is partly a rebound from a -4% FY2025 base and partly renminbi strength, so the underlying unit recovery is smaller than the reported rate.
rows.implication: Geographic concentration in Greater China ($64,839M, 17.8% of 9M revenue) is a swing factor for both revenue and the political risk premium.
rows.confidence: high on the segment figures, medium on the decomposition
rows.follow_up: What share of Greater China growth was price/mix versus units, and how exposed is the supply chain to tariffs on China-assembled devices?

plan.decision_question: How does Apple actually make money, and how durable are those economics?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple monetises the same customer twice — a 40%-gross-margin hardware sale that is paid for before the cost is incurred, then a 76%-gross-margin services annuity sold into an installed base of over 2.5 billion devices — and the durability of that second leg, not the first, is what a 39x multiple is paying for.
plan.why_different: This section prices the revenue model and the unit economics: product-line mix, the products-versus-services gross-margin bridge, a per-device waterfall, take rates and working capital. Demand, rivals and capability belong to the market, competition and technology sections.
plan.mechanism: Negative-working-capital hardware funds the balance sheet; the installed base converts into near-zero-CAC services at 76% gross margin; the two contested tolls (App Store commission and search default rent) sit inside that annuity.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own FY2023-FY2025 history for mix and margin; Samsung Electronics device division (Q3 2026 operating loss) for handset economics; Microsoft FY2026 gross margin 67.9% for the software-margin ceiling; Alphabet for platform take rates.
plan.counter_evidence: Services share of revenue fell in 2026 as hardware outgrew it; product gross margin is boosted by one-off tariff refunds while memory costs rise at triple-digit rates; the App Store link-out commission was vacated and the search deal is now a 12-month re-bid.
plan.visual: Unit economics table per active device per year, plus a pricing and take-rate table.
plan.prohibited: huge market, strong team, high barriers to entry, clear business model, fierce competition, well positioned, ecosystem moat unless evidenced, world-class, best-in-class

rows.finding: TTM to 2026-06-27: operating cash flow $146,724M, capex $10,041M, free cash flow $136,683M, net income $128,930M — conversion 1.06x on capex of 2.2% of revenue.
rows.mechanism: Assembly is outsourced and the tooling is owned by suppliers, so growth needs almost no capital; the cash thrown off goes to buybacks rather than to plant.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft FY2026: FCF/net income 0.50x, capex 39.2% of revenue. Alphabet TTM: 0.08x, capex 33.9%. Apple FY2025: 0.88x.
rows.weakens: Nine-month operating cash flow rose 43% ($116,996M from $81,754M) while net income rose 20%, so part of the record is a working-capital and tax-timing release that will not repeat; FY2025 conversion was only 0.88x.
rows.implication: Cash conversion is not the risk in this multiple; the risk is that the market pays 39x earnings (2.5% free-cash-flow yield) for a business whose growth is cyclical.
rows.confidence: high — filed statements for all three companies
rows.follow_up: What is the capex plan for AI infrastructure, and does Apple intend to fund data centres directly rather than through partners?

rows.finding: Q3 FY2026 gross margin of 50.1% included about 2 percentage points from tariff refunds worth $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS; nine-month products gross margin was 39.9% against 36.9% a year earlier, attributed to mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by higher costs including memory.
rows.mechanism: A tariff refund reverses a cost already expensed, so it lifts margin without any pricing action; memory inflation then works the other way with a lag of two to three quarters.
rows.benchmark: FY2023 44.1%, FY2024 46.2%, FY2025 46.9% — the 2026 level is 3 points above any prior year.
rows.weakens: Management expects component supply and cost pressure to intensify, and Samsung reports memory prices still rising across applications with 2027 demand expected to exceed supply.
rows.implication: Model a 47-48% gross margin, not 50%; 200 basis points off TTM gross margin is about $0.52 of EPS, or 6% of the $8.72 TTM figure.
rows.confidence: high on the disclosed items, medium on the normalised level
rows.follow_up: How much of the refund is still to come in the December quarter, and what memory cost is locked in for FY2027?

rows.finding: The FY2024 effective tax rate of 24.1% carried the State Aid Decision, and the FY2025 provision fell $10.7bn year over year on that base effect; normalising FY2024 to the FY2025 rate lifts FY2024 net income to about $104.2bn, cutting FY2025 EPS growth from a reported 22.7% to roughly 10%.
rows.mechanism: A one-off European Commission State Aid charge depressed FY2024 earnings and simultaneously inflated the next year's growth rate — a base effect, not a change in earning power.
rows.weakens: The nine-month FY2026 rate of 17.6% is already higher than FY2025 and FY2023, so the tax line has stopped flattering reported growth.
rows.implication: Do not extrapolate the 20%+ EPS growth of FY2025 into FY2027; the underlying rate was nearer 10% and the tax line is now a headwind.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is the sustainable ETR under the OECD Pillar Two rules, and does the FY2026 10-K disclose a new unrecognised tax benefit?

rows.finding: Nine months to 2026-06-27: buybacks $62,094M plus dividends $11,778M, or 67% of free cash flow of $110,197M, while net cash rose to $62,173M from $33,763M and debt fell to $84,344M from $98,657M; diluted shares fell 1.7% (15,005M to 14,750M) against net income growth of 20.0%, so buybacks added only about 2.4 points of the 22.4% EPS growth.
rows.mechanism: Buybacks lift EPS only in proportion to shares retired; at $344.63 a $62bn programme retires about 1.7% of the count, so the earnings matter more than the shrink.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 distributions were 107% of FCF; FY2024 101%; FY2023 93%.
rows.weakens: Repurchases at an average of roughly $244 a share in the nine months were accretive against today's $344.63, but a repeat at 39x earnings is far less value-creating than the 2023-2024 programmes.
rows.implication: The buyback is not debt-funded and not the main driver of EPS, which removes one of the bear-case pillars; the corollary is that Apple is now under-distributing and building a cash buffer.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Will the $100bn authorisation be spent at 39x earnings, and has the board raised the dividend again in 2026?

rows.finding: At 2026-06-27 cash and marketable securities totalled $146,517M against debt of $84,344M, a net cash position of $62,173M — 39% of total assets; the FY2025 notes carried $91.3bn of principal with $12.4bn due within 12 months and $37.0bn of future interest, and other income turned to +$670M in the nine months from -$698M.
rows.mechanism: Fixed-rate debt raised at low coupons is cheaper than the yield on the securities it holds only if the cash is genuinely strategic; here the spread is negative, so the debt is a tax and repatriation artefact rather than leverage.
rows.benchmark: Net cash was $33,763M at 2025-09-27 and $65,797M at 2021-09-25; debt peaked at $124,719M in FY2021.
rows.weakens: Unrealised losses of $2,604M on the securities portfolio (adjusted cost $148,631M against $146,517M fair value) mean the cash is slightly impaired if liquidated early, and $5.0bn of intangibles are current assets.
rows.implication: There is no refinancing or coverage risk; the balance sheet is a strategic asset that lets Apple absorb a memory cycle or a regulatory fine without diluting.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is the weighted-average coupon and maturity profile after the 2026 repayments, and are any notes callable?

rows.finding: Management states there is not at least a reasonable possibility of a material loss on asserted claims, carrying no disclosed accrual, while the DMA allows fines up to 10% of worldwide net sales and the Epic contempt finding is before the Supreme Court in the term that began in October 2026.
rows.mechanism: Antitrust remedies bite the take rate rather than the headcount, so a small percentage change in commission flows almost entirely to operating income.
rows.benchmark: The April 2025 DMA fine was EUR500M; the statutory ceiling is 10% of worldwide net sales.
rows.weakens: Apple has a long record of absorbing single-digit-billion fines without a visible earnings effect, and the remedies so far have been conduct-based rather than structural.
rows.implication: Treat the legal tail as a separate, unaccrued liability of low single-digit billions a year rather than as a base-case deduction — it is a sizing question for a watchlist entry price.
rows.confidence: medium — the exposure is unquantified by the company
rows.follow_up: Has the Supreme Court scheduled argument in No. 25-1311, and what commission did the district court set on remand for link-out purchases?

plan.decision_question: Are earnings quality and cash conversion as strong as the multiple implies?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's profit is unusually cash-true — trailing-twelve-month free cash flow of $136.7bn is 1.06x net income with capex at 2.2% of revenue, against 0.50x at Microsoft and 0.08x at Alphabet — but the FY2026 records are flattered by roughly $2bn of tariff refunds, a working-capital release and a 17.6% tax rate, so the quality sits in the model, not in the growth rate the multiple is paying for.
plan.why_different: This section rebuilds the statements and notes and tests quality of earnings, returns and capital allocation; the multiple, the demand outlook and the legal exposure are handled by the valuation, market and regulatory sections.
plan.mechanism: An asset-light, negative-working-capital model with outsourced assembly converts nearly all net income into free cash, so the multiple is a claim on durability and growth rather than on conversion; the swing variables are product gross margin (memory), the tax rate and the pace of buybacks, not capex or leverage.
plan.comparison_set: Microsoft FY2026 (capex 39.2% of revenue, FCF/NI 0.50x, gross margin 67.9%) and Alphabet TTM (capex 33.9%, FCF/NI 0.08x) for the AI-capex contrast; Apple's own FY2023-FY2025 conversion and margin history; a ~10% cost of equity against a 2.5% earnings yield.
plan.counter_evidence: About $2bn of Q3 FY2026 gross profit and $0.11 of EPS came from tariff refunds; memory input costs are rising at triple-digit rates and management expects the trend to intensify; the FY2024 tax one-off makes FY2025 growth look better than it was; no accrual is carried against DMA or DOJ antitrust exposure.
plan.visual: Financial statements table (FY2023-FY2025, nine months FY2026, TTM), returns and working-capital table, and one info warning on the quality of the FY2026 margin record.
plan.prohibited: huge market, strong team, high barriers to entry, clear business model, fierce competition, well positioned, risks are manageable, clean balance sheet without the good-will caveat

rows.finding: IDC forecasts 2026 smartphone shipments at just over 1.0B units (-16.7%, steepest annual fall on record) while market value rises 6.3% to $613B and ASP rises 27.6% to $581.
rows.mechanism: NAND/DRAM costs up more than 300% YoY are passed through to shelf prices, so dollars grow while units fall; the sub-$100 segment (173M units in 2025) fell ~60% in Q2 2026 and emerging markets are forecast down over 20%.
rows.benchmark: 2025: ~1.26B units, +2% (Counterpoint); 2026 value $613B vs bottom-up 1.0B x $581 = $581B.
rows.weakens: Demand destruction and affordability limits mean the value growth is cost-driven, not a healthy cycle; it can reverse when memory normalises in 2028.
rows.implication: Apple revenue growth must come from price/mix and share, not market volume; do not capitalise 2026 growth as a trend.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What share of Apple's FY2026 iPhone growth is units versus price/mix?

rows.finding: Premium handsets (wholesale ASP $600+) reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026, up from 25% in H1 2025 and 20% in H1 2022; Apple took 65% of premium units with 9% growth.
rows.mechanism: Rising memory costs push the whole market up-price, mechanically expanding the premium segment and concentrating value in the vendor with the strongest premium brand.
rows.benchmark: Apple global unit share 20% in 2025 (Counterpoint); IDC expects iOS share to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android falls 24.3%.
rows.weakens: The premium-share gain is partly inflation of the price boundary, not Apple winning new buyers at constant prices.
rows.implication: Apple's value capture is durable but cyclical; the franchise is pricing power, and it is being tested by a 20-30% price increase.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: Does premium unit growth continue if ASPs rise again in 2027?

rows.finding: Greater China shipments were ~66M units in Q2 2026 (-4.3%, fifth straight decline), with Apple at 18.1% and Huawei at 22.6%; IDC expects the decline to widen to ~20% in H2 2026 and recovery only in 2028-2029.
rows.mechanism: A shrinking pool plus a resurgent local champion means share gains do not compound; Apple's price hold and pull-forward ahead of H2 price rises flattered Q2.
rows.benchmark: Apple Greater China revenue +30% in 9M FY2026 (company filing) against a market down 4.2% in H1 2026.
rows.weakens: The +30% China revenue growth is not a durable market recovery; it is share gain plus timing in a declining market.
rows.implication: Treat China as the swing risk to the growth story; H2 FY2026 and FY2027 comps are the test.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: How much of the China revenue surge was pull-forward ahead of price increases?

rows.finding: Wearables: ~148M units in Q2 2026 (+2.7%); Apple 15.5% share, Xiaomi 11.7%, Huawei 10.9%; 2026 forecast ~625M units (+1.7%) and a 2.4% CAGR to ~687M units by 2030, with smartwatches -3.7% in 2026 and glasses +35.2%.
rows.mechanism: Category mix is shifting toward glasses and rings, where Apple is not the leader; smartwatches and wristbands are shrinking.
rows.benchmark: Apple's share was 21.0% in Q4 2025 and 18.9% in Q3 2025; Huawei leads smartwatches at 18.8% vs Apple 17.2%.
rows.weakens: Wearables cannot be underwritten as a second growth engine to 2030.
rows.implication: Value the wearables segment as a low-growth attachment business, not a re-rating driver.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Will Apple enter AI glasses before 2028, and at what price?

rows.finding: Services pools are large but contested: global advertising $1.34T in 2026 (+11.9%), App Store ecosystem billings ~$1.4T in 2025 of which ~$149B digital goods commissionable, and Apple services revenue $120.5B TTM (+14.1% in 9M FY2026).
rows.mechanism: Apple monetises a small slice of advertising and a large slice of app digital goods; growth comes from installed-base monetisation and price, not from a growing addressable market alone.
rows.benchmark: Spotify has 300M paying subscribers vs Apple Music's estimated 100-108M; Alphabet's total revenue is $471B TTM, nearly four times Apple's services.
rows.weakens: Services growth is partly price- and commission-driven, and the EU DMA cuts the take rate on external distribution to 5% from October 2026.
rows.implication: Services can grow low-to-mid teens for now, but the terminal take rate is regulated downward in Europe.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: What is the revenue-per-installed-device trend excluding price increases?

rows.finding: The PC market fell 4.9% to 68.2M units in Q2 2026 while Apple grew Mac shipments 10.1% to 9.9% share, behind Lenovo 24.4%, HP 19.1% and Dell 13.6%.
rows.mechanism: Apple gains share in a shrinking, price-inflating market through new models (MacBook Neo) and vertical integration of silicon.
rows.benchmark: Mac revenue $33.7B in FY2025, 8.1% of Apple revenue; +9% in 9M FY2026.
rows.weakens: Mac is too small to move group growth, and IDC sees a sharp H2 2026 slowdown as price rises bite.
rows.implication: Mac is a share-gainer and margin supporter, not the growth thesis.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Does Mac share hold when PC prices rise again in 2027?

rows.finding: Policy changes the market's economics: EU DMA terms from 2026-10-01 cut commissions to 26% for in-app purchase, 20% for alternative payments and 5% for apps distributed outside the App Store; US tariffs moved twice in 2026 (IEEPA tariffs struck down 2026-02-20, Section 301 duties imposed, Section 232 review imposed no additional tariffs on Apple products on 2026-01-14).
rows.mechanism: Regulation lowers the platform take rate in Europe and adds cost volatility in the US, directly changing services gross margin and product cost.
rows.benchmark: Headline App Store commission outside the EU remains 30%/15%; the EU external-distribution rate is 5%.
rows.weakens: The view that Apple's services margin is structurally protected.
rows.implication: Apply a lower terminal take rate to EU services and a tariff risk premium to US hardware cost.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What share of services revenue is EU App Store commission, and how fast will developers shift distribution?

rows.implication: Current 39.5x is a 27% premium to the four-year mean of 31.0x and the highest EV/Sales in five years: the price already assumes improvement, so the margin of safety is negative.
rows.confidence: high - SEC XBRL plus timestamped Yahoo quotes
rows.follow_up: What is the FY2027 consensus EPS and revenue, and how much of FY2026 growth is tariff front-running?

rows.finding: Services gross margin 76.0% and products 39.1% on TTM revenue of $120.5bn services and $346.3bn products; consolidated gross margin 48.7% TTM and 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter (including ~2pp of tariff refunds).
rows.mechanism: Every 100bp of mix shift toward services adds roughly 37bp to consolidated gross margin at constant segment margins, which is why a hardware company reports software-like gross margins.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 services gross margin 75.4% ($82.3bn on $109.2bn) versus products 36.8%; consolidated 46.9% in FY2025.
rows.weakens: Apple does not disclose segment operating income, so services profitability is an estimate; the 2pp tariff-refund benefit will not repeat.
rows.implication: The services mix is the single largest support for the multiple; any regulatory or competitive hit to services margins moves the whole valuation, not just one segment.
rows.confidence: high for gross profit by segment (filing); medium for operating profit by segment (estimated allocation)
rows.follow_up: What share of services gross profit comes from App Store commission and from the Google default-search payment?

rows.finding: Nine-month FY2026 operating cash flow $116,996m versus $81,754m a year earlier; of the $35,242m increase, $25,177m is a favourable swing in 'other current and non-current liabilities' (+$10,016m versus -$15,161m) and $2,631m is receivables.
rows.mechanism: Working-capital and accrual timing, not earnings, produced most of the cash-flow step-up, so trailing FCF overstates recurring cash generation.
rows.benchmark: TTM FCF $136.7bn (2.7% yield) versus a working-capital-normalised $111.5bn (2.2% yield, 45x) - my estimate; FY2025 FCF was $98.8bn.
rows.weakens: The 10-Q aggregates the liability line, so the reversal timing is unknown and part may be structural (deferred revenue, accrued taxes).
rows.implication: On normalised FCF the shares are 45x, not 37x; the buyback and the DCF must be run on the lower number.
rows.confidence: medium - the swing is disclosed, its composition is not
rows.follow_up: What sits inside the $25.2bn other-liabilities swing, and does it reverse in FY2027?

rows.finding: June 2026 quarter revenue $109,417m, +16.4% y/y; iPhone $54,252m (+21.7%), Services $30,739m (+12.1%), Greater China $18,816m (+22.4%); diluted EPS $2.02 (+28.7%) including $0.11 from tariff refunds.
rows.mechanism: A hardware upgrade cycle plus a China recovery re-accelerated revenue far above the FY2023-FY2025 trend, which is the fundamental case for a premium multiple.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 revenue growth +6.4%, FY2024 +2.0%, FY2023 -2.8%; TTM revenue $466.8bn (+12.2%).
rows.weakens: One quarter; iPhone and China are the most cyclical lines and the easiest to have been pulled forward by tariff timing.
rows.implication: The growth-to-GDP bear case is contradicted for now; the question is whether 16% is a cycle peak that the 39.5x multiple capitalises as permanent.
rows.confidence: high - company's own 8-K press release
rows.follow_up: What is the iPhone unit versus price/mix split in the June quarter, and what does the September quarter guide to?

rows.finding: Peer multiples at 2026-10-30: Apple 39.5x P/E and 32.1x EV/EBIT; Microsoft 27.3x and 23.6x; Alphabet 14.6x and 21.2x; Meta 21.0x and 19.9x; Amazon 19.4x and 25.5x; Dell 24.7x and 21.0x; HP 11.0x and 9.6x; median of the six 20.2x P/E and 20.5x EV/EBIT.
rows.mechanism: Apple's premium is a quality and duration premium: higher margins and returns than hardware peers, lower growth than the platform peers, and a more concentrated product line than either.

rows.finding: DCF on FY2026E revenue of $477.0bn (my estimate from nine months' actual plus a $112.7bn fourth quarter), growth of 9%/8%/7%/6%/5%, 33% operating margin, 17.5% tax and capex 3.0% versus D&A 2.8%: equity value $229/share at an 8.5% WACC, $302 at 7.5%, $352 at 7.0%, $193 at 9.5%.
rows.mechanism: Nearly all of the valuation sits in the terminal value, so the answer is driven by the spread between WACC and terminal growth rather than by the near-term forecast.
rows.benchmark: The market price of $344.63 is matched at roughly a 7.0% WACC; my cost of equity from a 4.93% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a 1.05 beta is 9.7%.
rows.weakens: The cost of equity is an assumption; a 7% WACC (which some quality-growth models use) makes the current price fair rather than expensive.
rows.implication: The shares are fairly valued only if the required return is about 7%; at a defensible 9.0-9.5% cost of equity the DCF says $193-$212, a 38-44% downside.
rows.confidence: medium - inputs are disclosed, the discount rate is a judgement
rows.follow_up: What WACC does management's own capital-allocation hurdle imply, and does the buyback clear it at 39.5x?

rows.finding: Sum of the parts: services EBIT of $62.7bn (76.0% gross margin less 40% of corporate opex, an estimate) at 23x = $1,442bn; hardware EBIT of $92.1bn at 12x = $1,105bn; plus $62.2bn net cash = $2,609bn, or $177/share.
rows.mechanism: Applying market multiples to Apple's own segment margins, rather than to its consolidated earnings, strips out the scarcity premium the market pays for a single $5tn liquid compounder.
rows.benchmark: HP at 9.6x EV/EBIT and Dell at 21.0x for hardware; Microsoft at 23.6x and Meta at 19.9x for platform services.
rows.weakens: Segment EBIT is not disclosed, so the allocation of $72.3bn of opex is an assumption; a 60/40 split toward services raises the SOTP to about $194/share, still far below the market.
rows.implication: The market is paying about twice what the parts are worth at peer multiples - the gap is a liquidity and quality premium that can compress without any operating deterioration.
rows.confidence: medium - gross profit is filed, opex allocation is estimated
rows.follow_up: What multiple would a strategic or activist ascribe to services if App Store commission economics were halved?

rows.finding: Capital return: $82.2bn of buybacks and $15.6bn of dividends in the TTM to 2026-06-27, a 1.9% total shareholder yield; diluted shares 16,865m in FY2021 to 14,715m in the June 2026 quarter.
rows.mechanism: Buybacks at 39.5x earnings buy a 2.5% earnings yield, below the 4.93% risk-free rate and well below the cost of equity, so repurchases shrink the share count without creating value at this price.
rows.benchmark: Five-year revenue CAGR 5.0%, net income CAGR 6.4%, diluted EPS CAGR 9.2% - roughly 2.8 points a year of EPS growth came from the shrinking share count, not from operations.
rows.weakens: The buyback is price-sensitive: the same dollar amount retires 3.4% of the shares at $250 versus 1.7% at $345, so a de-rating mechanically raises future EPS growth.
rows.implication: Roughly 30% of historic EPS growth is financial engineering; if the buyback slows or the multiple compresses, the EPS growth that supports the valuation loses a leg.
rows.confidence: high - all figures from the filings
rows.follow_up: At what price does management slow the repurchase, and will the May 2027 authorisation be larger than $100bn?

plan.decision_question: What is Apple worth today, and what price makes it an attractive long for a long-only fund?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple is an exceptional franchise priced as a perpetual compounder: at $344.63 the market capitalises $128.1bn of NOPAT at 38.8x, which requires about 6.9% perpetual growth or a 7.0% cost of capital, so a long-only buyer is accepting a ~7% expected return on a business whose own five-year revenue CAGR is 5.0%.
plan.why_different: This section is the only one that converts the operating story into a price: it owns the arithmetic of what the market is paying, the DCF, the sum of the parts and the entry threshold, and it must state a number at which the shares become a buy.
plan.mechanism: Apple's value is the present value of a slowly compounding cash flow with a very long duration; when the ten-year Treasury is 4.93% and the cost of equity is ~9.5%, the multiple the market pays (39.5x) discounts a 7% return, so the shares de-rate until either the discount rate falls or growth rises. Buybacks recycle cash at a 2.5% earnings yield and therefore support EPS without creating value at this price.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own FY2022-FY2025 year-end multiples (24.6x, 27.9x, 37.5x, 34.2x; four-year mean 31.0x), US platform peers (MSFT 27.3x, GOOGL 14.6x, META 21.0x, AMZN 19.4x on P/E; 19.9x-25.5x on EV/EBIT), hardware peers (HP 11.0x, Dell 24.7x P/E; 9.6x and 21.0x EV/EBIT) and a 9.0-9.5% cost of equity against a 4.93% ten-year Treasury.
plan.counter_evidence: Growth re-accelerated to +16.4% in the June 2026 quarter with a 50.1% gross margin, so the DCF's 9%-to-5% fade may understate the cycle; a 7% WACC (defensible in some quality-growth models) makes $344.63 fair; and the buyback's price sensitivity cushions any de-rating. Alphabet's 14.6x P/E also drags the peer median down and exaggerates Apple's premium.
plan.visual: Valuation methods table (method, inputs, value per share, weight) plus a WACC x terminal-growth sensitivity grid showing the market price is reached only near a 7% WACC.
plan.prohibited: No 'about 5', no 'strong moat', no 'well positioned', no 'huge', no unlabelled estimates, no claim that the DCF is precise, no repetition of the risk section's regulatory narrative beyond its valuation effect.

rows.mechanism: Almost all of Apple's value is terminal, so a 50bp change in the discount rate moves value 15-18% - the valuation is a rates call on a quality cash flow.
rows.benchmark: Cost of equity built from the 4.93% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a 1.05 beta; 7.5-9.5% sensitivity grid.
rows.weakens: The cost of equity is a judgement, not an observation; at 7.0% the base case matches the market price.
rows.implication: Buy below roughly $270 for a 9% three-year return, or wait for evidence that EPS grows above 12%.
rows.confidence: medium - arithmetic high, discount rate contested
rows.follow_up: What equity risk premium does the market imply for Apple, and has the ten-year yield moved since 2026-10-30?

rows.finding: Sum of the parts: services EBIT of $62.7bn at 23x plus hardware EBIT of $92.1bn at 12x plus $62.2bn net cash is $177 a share, or $238 at 28x and 18x.
rows.mechanism: The gap between the parts and the market price is a single-security and liquidity premium paid for one of the largest, most liquid compounders.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft 23.6x EV/EBIT for the services leg, HP 9.6x and Dell 21.0x for the hardware leg; four-year mean P/E 31.0x for the whole company.
rows.weakens: Services at a 76.0% gross margin could justify more than 23x, and the allocation of the $72.3bn operating expense 40/60 is an estimate.
rows.implication: A break-up or activist route would have to close a $107-168 per share gap, which no disclosed campaign attempts.
rows.confidence: medium - segment EBIT is an allocation, not a disclosed figure
rows.follow_up: What EBIT margin does Apple disclose or imply for services, rather than the allocated estimate?

rows.finding: Trailing FCF of $136,683M carries $14,101M from other current and non-current liabilities (+$10,016M in the nine months to 2026-06-27 and $4,085M in the September 2025 quarter); netting the line to zero or to its $2,502M three-year average gives normalised FCF of $122.6-125.1bn, 0.95-0.97x net income, a 2.4-2.5% yield and about 41x P/FCF.
rows.mechanism: The accrual is not repeatable earnings: either it is a working-capital build that reverses, or deferred consideration for $13,270M of gross intangibles added, in which case the cash is an unpaid purchase.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft FCF yield 1.5%, Alphabet 0.6%, peer median 2.5%; the earlier $111.5bn figure subtracted the full $25,177M year-on-year swing and so double-counted the prior-year State Aid settlement, which is not in the trailing period.
