rows.belief: Replacement demand is mature and price-led: buyers upgrade for battery, camera and now AI, but a 27.6% ASP increase is the live test of willingness to pay.
rows.evidence: Global 2026 smartphone units fall 16.7% to just over 1.0B while value rises 6.3% to $613B and ASP rises 27.6% to $581; Apple's iPhone revenue rose 22.4% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 against that market [S84, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: IDC attributes part of the China strength to purchases pulled forward ahead of Apple's own second-half 2026 price rises and sees China's decline widening to 20% in H2 2026; the sub-$100 segment fell nearly 60% in Q2 2026 [S84, S87].
rows.confidence: medium-high
rows.change: Discounting or a lower-capacity model to hold volume, or a December 2026 quarter that shows unit and mix elasticity.

rows.belief: The moat is real in silicon and the operating system and rented in AI: the intelligence layer protects the franchise without widening it.
rows.evidence: 2nm A20 Pro and in-house C2 modem, 65% of premium phone units, 40.1% product gross margin in the June 2026 quarter (39.9% for the nine months); Siri AI shipped 2026-09-14 as an English beta on a licensed Gemini model confirmed 2026-01-12 [S113, S94, S17, S111].
rows.counter_evidence: The flagship feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's TPUs; U.S. patent grants fell 12% to 2,722 in 2025 and no blocking family was verified [S118, S117].
rows.confidence: high on hardware, low on AI
rows.change: Siri exits beta with usage evidence that Apple's integration beats standalone assistants, or a second slip in availability.

rows.belief: 2026 is a price re-pricing cycle, not a growth cycle; the base rate for revenue is mid-single digits.
rows.evidence: Revenue compounded 3.3% a year FY2021-FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and 5.0% to the last twelve months; the 2026 acceleration is iPhone price/mix and China share gain [S5, S6, S84].
rows.counter_evidence: Foldables could add more than 17M units by 2027 at a $2,550+ ASP, 40% of a $45.7B category, and an AI upgrade cycle could pull demand forward [S84].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Two consecutive quarters of unit growth in a stable-ASP market.

rows.belief: Distribution scales without new capital: 40% direct and 60% indirect, with India at 25% of assembly and six stores.
rows.evidence: FY2025 net sales of $416,161M at 40/60 direct/indirect; 55M iPhones assembled in India in 2025 against 36M; India sales above $9B [S5, S115].
rows.counter_evidence: Indian assembly and components still cost more than China or Vietnam, and smartphone production subsidies expired on 2026-03-31 [S115].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Renewal of India's production incentives or evidence of cost parity with China.

rows.belief: The best unit economics in hardware: negative working capital bolted to a 76.3% services annuity.
rows.evidence: TTM revenue $466,823M and gross profit $227,123M; services are 25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit and cover company R&D 2.1 times; cash conversion cycle of -56.8 days [S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Services fell to 25.2% of revenue from 26.2% as iPhone grew faster, and two services tolls, the App Store commission and the search licence, are being repriced in court [S6, S69, S70].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Services growth below 10% for two quarters or a structural cut in the App Store take rate.

rows.belief: The bench is deep and insider-built in hardware, operations and finance, and thin and newly reorganised in AI.
rows.evidence: Ternus became CEO on 2026-09-01 with Cook Executive Chair; the CFO (2025-01-01) and COO (2025) were internal promotions; 92% say-on-pay; AI moved under Federighi on 2025-12-01 [S56, S11, S127].
rows.counter_evidence: No filing names an owner of the AI P&L; Srouji was named Chief Hardware Officer on 2026-04-20, which supersedes the December 2025 departure report but leaves key-person concentration with no disclosed successor; the general counsel changed in 2026-03 while the DOJ and DMA cases are live [S133, S141, S132].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A disclosed AI leader with P&L ownership, or the loss of Srouji without a named successor.

rows.belief: Not attractive at this price: the franchise is exceptional, the multiple is not.
rows.evidence: 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 20.2x peer median, and 32.1x EV/EBIT against 20.5x; the DCF is $277 at 8.5% on a 35% margin, $212 at 9.0% on 33% and $133 at 9.5% on 30%; the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0% [S7, S14, S6, S10].
rows.counter_evidence: Forward 35.2x is in line with its own twelve-month forward average of 35.7x, and a 148.8% return on equity has historically held a premium multiple [S7, S6].
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic, medium on the intrinsic-value gap
rows.change: A de-rating to about $270, or evidence of EPS growth above 12% into FY2027-28.

rows.belief: The exit is the public market and the buyback: liquidity risk is nil, multiple risk is everything.
rows.evidence: 40.41M shares and $13.84B trade daily; no peer is large enough to acquire Apple; the three-year IRR is -3.2% to +4.5% across 27-34x exits on a 1.94% shareholder yield [S7, S14, S6, S97].
rows.counter_evidence: A reversion to the 31.0x four-year mean from 35.2x forward costs 11.9% of the price, about 4.1% a year over three years, and the same daily liquidity is the channel that de-rates in a broad sell-off [S7, S97].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A sustained multiple above 45x forward, about $440, would be a sale condition rather than a buy signal.

rows.belief: The shares trade above a defensible intrinsic value and above every point of the DCF grid.
rows.evidence: $344.63 on 2026-10-30 against $277 at 8.5% on a 35% margin, $212 at 9.0% on 33% and $133 at 9.5% on 30%; the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0% and $193 at 9.5%/4.0%; sum of the parts $177-238; the own-history multiple implies $303 [S7, S6, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: The bull operating case at 8.5% reaches $277, and a 4.93% ten-year Treasury makes a lower discount rate defensible for some buyers, but no grid point on the base operating case reaches the price [S6, S10].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A fall in the ten-year yield toward 4.0%, or long-term growth proven above 6%.

rows.belief: Cash-true but flattered at the margin by tariff refunds and by buybacks.
rows.evidence: Normalised free cash flow covers net income 0.97 times at the centre of a 0.95-0.99x band on capex of 2.2% of revenue, against 0.50x at Microsoft and 0.08x at Alphabet; buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% nine-month EPS growth [S6, S49, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: The 50.1% June-quarter gross margin includes 2 points of one-off tariff refunds worth $0.11 of $2.02 EPS, and FY2025 returned 107% of free cash flow [S17, S5].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A December-quarter guide below 48% gross margin, a slowdown in repurchases, or a FY2026 10-K that confirms the other-liabilities swing is an unpaid purchase.

rows.belief: Conversion is structurally strong, but the trailing figure overstates the run-rate by a working-capital swing that is partly an Irish tax artefact.
rows.evidence: $136,683M of TTM free cash flow; nine-month operating cash flow rose $35,176M, with other current and non-current liabilities at +$10,016M against -$15,161M a year earlier; the line's clean three-year average is $2,502M, so normalised free cash flow is $122.6-127.3B with $125.1B central, 0.97x conversion, a 2.4-2.5% yield and 40.2x price to free cash flow on the basic market value (40.5x diluted) [S6, S7].
rows.counter_evidence: The normalisation is an analyst estimate, not a filed figure; a $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities against $13,270M of gross intangibles added is consistent with deferred consideration for intangibles, which puts free cash flow at $123.2B, inside the band at 40.8x on the basic market value [S6].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: The FY2026 10-K working-capital and intangible detail due with the 2026-11-02 results.

rows.belief: A fortress: net cash, no debt-funded buyback, manageable maturities.
rows.evidence: Cash and marketable securities of $146,517M against debt of $84,344M, net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M while $62,094M of stock was retired; $12.4B of debt due within twelve months [S6, S5].
rows.counter_evidence: $2,604M of unrealised securities losses, $57.0B of purchase obligations and $16.8B of lease commitments [S6, S5].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A move to net debt, or repurchases funded by new issuance.

rows.belief: Our reading is that the price capitalises the 2026 margin as a base; we expect it to normalise. That is an assumption about the price, not a sourced consensus estimate.
rows.evidence: Guidance of 9-11% revenue growth for the September quarter; consensus iPhone revenue of $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4%) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%), with no group-revenue or gross-margin consensus held; our base underwrites 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1% [S71, S72, S6, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: Management beat guidance through FY2026 and launched the iPhone 18 Pro and Duo into the holiday quarter [S17, S113].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A December-quarter guide at or above 49% gross margin with FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices.

rows.belief: The next twelve months are event-dense and mostly adversarial for the multiple.
rows.evidence: Q4 FY2026 results on 2026-11-02; the DMA fee schedule in force from 2026-10-01; Supreme Court review of link-out fees after certiorari on 2026-06-30; the Google remedy appeal likely in 2027; standard iPhone 18 in spring 2027 [S77, S79, S76, S112].
rows.counter_evidence: There are positive catalysts too: Siri out of beta in five more languages from October 2026 and the spring 2027 iPhone cycle [S113, S112].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: An appellate ruling or settlement that removes the search-payment tail.

rows.belief: Zero today; a first tranche at $270 or below, a second at $245, and the 5% cap only below $225.
rows.evidence: A 9% three-year return needs an entry near $270; $1B is 7.2% of one day's traded value; the realistic bear drawdown is 30% to $241; the full Kelly on the scenario inputs is 337% of the fund, so the 5% cap is a risk-budget limit rather than a sizing output [S7, S6, S97].
rows.counter_evidence: The discipline has been wrong before: the shares returned 27.5% in twelve months, and a valuation-based sale would have missed it [S7, S97].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A de-rating to $270, or a December-quarter guide at or above 49% with memory contracted.

scenarios.driver: The AI upgrade cycle and the foldable Duo extend the iPhone cycle into FY2027-28; services growth stays above 15%; gross margin holds 48% through the memory cycle; the search payment survives at a lower rate.
scenarios.evidence: iPhone revenue rose 22.4% in nine months; iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max list at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable Duo launched 2026-09-09; IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at a $2,550+ ASP [S6, S113, S84].
scenarios.outcome: FY2027 EPS of $10.20 at 35x gives $357, +4% price and about +4.3% total return over twelve months; the DCF at an 8.5% cost of equity on a 35% margin and 14% initial growth is $277; a three-year IRR of up to +9% needs a 34x exit.
scenarios.implication: Own it, but the upside comes from a multiple that stays elevated, not from a margin of safety at entry.

scenarios.driver: Growth fades from 9% to 5%, gross margin normalises to 47-48% as memory costs reset, services grows 12-14%, and the search payment is renegotiated lower.
scenarios.evidence: The DCF is $212 at a 9.0% cost of equity on a 33% margin and 9% initial growth; the 31.0x four-year mean P/E implies $303 on FY2027 EPS of $9.79; revenue compounded 3.3% a year FY2021-25 and 5.0% to the last twelve months [S6, S10, S7, S97].
scenarios.outcome: $284 at 29x FY2027 EPS of $9.79, -18% price and -17.7% total return; the DCF is $212 at 9.0% (33% margin) and $277 at 8.5% (35%); the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0%; the three-year IRR is 1.3% at a 31x exit.
scenarios.implication: Do not own at $344.63: the compounding is real but already paid for, and the three-year return is roughly the shareholder yield.

scenarios.driver: Memory costs break the hardware margin below 46%, services growth falls under 8% as the DMA and link-out remedies bite, and the search payment is cut or banned on appeal.
scenarios.evidence: The iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials is up 38% year on year with memory 34% of it; the Ninth Circuit affirmed civil contempt on 2025-12-11; the DOJ cross-appeal seeks a payment ban; losing $20B is 12.9% of EPS [S99, S79, S76, S6].
scenarios.outcome: $241 at 24.6x FY2027 EPS of $9.79, a 30% drawdown; the $133 DCF at a 9.5% cost of equity on 30% margins and 4% growth is the permanent-loss tail; three-year IRR -12% at a 27x exit.
scenarios.implication: The entry price has to price this: even from $270 the three-year return is only 5.0-13.3% across 27-34x exits, so size, not conviction, carries the risk.

assumptions.assumption: Gross margin normalises to 47-48%, not the 50.1% June-quarter print, as tariff refunds lapse and memory costs reset.
assumptions.disproof: A December 2026 quarter guided at or above 49% gross margin with FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices.
assumptions.impact: -6.0% EPS per 200 basis points of gross margin, and multiple compression on a peak-earnings read [S6, S17].
assumptions.early_warning: The 2026-11-02 guidance and TrendForce bill-of-materials data, where the iPhone 18 Pro BOM is up 38% with memory at 34% of it [S99, S72].

assumptions.assumption: The Google default-search payment survives the D.C. Circuit appeal, renegotiated lower rather than banned.
assumptions.disproof: An appellate ruling banning payments or capping them below the current economics.
assumptions.impact: A ban is -12.9% of EPS and about 15% of FY2025 operating income; a materially lower rate resets the services multiple [S6, S80].
assumptions.early_warning: D.C. Circuit briefing and decision expected in 2027; DOJ and state cross-appeal filed February 2026 [S76, S80].

assumptions.assumption: Services grows 12-14% without relying on hardware mix, and the EU take-rate cut does not accelerate.
assumptions.disproof: Two consecutive quarters of services growth below 10%, or faster migration to external distribution in the EU after 2026-10-01.
assumptions.impact: A 3-point cut in services growth removes roughly a tenth of the sum-of-the-parts value; each $1B of EU commission lost is $0.75B of gross profit [S78].
assumptions.early_warning: The quarterly services line and developer take-up of the 5% Core Technology Commission [S77, S6].

assumptions.assumption: The buyback continues at $80B a year or more with net cash positive, so EPS growth keeps its 2-3 point financial tailwind.
assumptions.disproof: A cut to the authorisation, or repurchases funded by new debt.
assumptions.impact: Buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% nine-month EPS growth; losing that cuts EPS growth to mid-single digits [S6, S17].
assumptions.early_warning: The May 2027 authorisation and the FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement [S5, S6].

assumptions.assumption: The Gemini licence stays an R&D expense and is not repriced per device or per query into services margin.
assumptions.disproof: Renewal terms disclosed that price the model per device or per query.
assumptions.impact: A $1B annual licence is 0.65% of TTM operating income and $0.06 of EPS; per-device pricing at $0.50/$1/$2 across 2.5B devices is $1.25B/$2.5B/$5.0B a year, $0.07/$0.14/$0.28 of EPS [S111, S73].
assumptions.early_warning: Renewal commentary from Apple or Google, and any services margin step-down unexplained by mix [S111].

consensus.consensus: The market pays 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings. Our reading is that the price capitalises the 2026 margin as a base; that is an assumption about what the price discounts, not a sourced consensus estimate, because no dated consensus gross-margin or group-revenue figure is in the register. The only consensus in the register is iPhone revenue: $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4%) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%).
consensus.our_view: Non-consensus on price, not on franchise: the business is a genuine compounder, but the 2026 margin is a peak and no point of the DCF grid reaches $344.63. The evidence supports a watchlist place and an entry near $270, not ownership at the current multiple.
consensus.evidence: The DCF is $277 at 8.5% on a 35% margin, $212 at 9.0% on 33% and $133 at 9.5% on 30%; the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0% and $193 at 9.5%/4.0%; the sum of the parts is $177-238; and the June-quarter margin carried 2 points of tariff refunds [S6, S10, S71, S72, S17].
consensus.proof_event: The December-quarter gross-margin guide on 2026-11-02, and the D.C. Circuit decision on the Google payments expected in 2027.

one_question.question: Will the Google default-search payment survive the D.C. Circuit appeal, and at what annual rate?
one_question.why: The payment, put at $20B in 2022 by the trial record, is 18.3% of FY2025 services revenue and about 15% of FY2025 operating income at near-pure margin. A ban or a materially lower rate resets the services multiple that carries most of the valuation, and it moves fair value from the base case toward the bear case regardless of how well the hardware cycle trades.

modules.position_sizing: Watchlist, zero position today. First tranche 0.75-1.0% of the fund at $270 or below, where a 9% three-year return becomes reachable across 27-34x exits; second tranche to 2.5-3.0% at $245; cap the position at 5% below $225. Maximum loss at the cap is 1.5% of the fund on the 30% drawdown; the full Kelly at $270 on the stated inputs is 337% of the fund, so the 5% cap is 1.5% of full Kelly and a risk-budget decision. Sell review above $380 (38.8x the FY2027 build); sell on valuation alone above 45x forward, about $440; sell outright on two quarters of sub-10% services growth, gross margin below 47%, or a structure that removes the search payment.

answers.most_damaging_fact: The survival and size of the Google search payment. The base case assumes it is renegotiated lower, not lost, but a D.C. Circuit ban is -10% to -13% of EPS and, with a services de-rating, -15% to -20% of value (sections 6 and 10, S70, S76, S135). The $20bn figure is a 2022 trial estimate, not a disclosure: if the 2026 payment is 25% larger, the EPS hit is about 16%. The second candidate is the gross-margin assumption: the base case capitalises 47-48%, while TrendForce has DRAM contract prices plus 10-15% in 4Q26 and NAND plus 15-20% with supply tight into 2027 (S136), and a 46% margin puts fair value at $270 at 29x, the entry price itself.
answers.company_only_claims: Five positive claims rest only on Apple material: the 2.5bn active installed base (an earnings-call figure, used for the per-device economics in section 6 and the per-device AI stress in section 10); the Gemini licence at about $1bn a year, which is reported and not confirmed by either company (S111); the Siri capability and Private Cloud Compute privacy claims (Apple Newsroom, S113, S127); the $1.4tn App Store ecosystem (S83); and the 'record installed base' and upgrade-cycle framing. Each is labelled as company-sourced in its section. The $20bn search payment is the opposite case: a litigated estimate, not a company disclosure, and therefore not a company claim.
answers.generic_section: Section 2 (Team) was the thinnest and has been corrected in revision 4: Srouji was named Chief Hardware Officer on 2026-04-20, adding Hardware Engineering to Hardware Technology (S133, confirmed by S141), superseding the December 2025 departure report (S131); what remains is thin disclosure, with no degrees for six of seven executives and AI accountability argued from the absence of disclosure. Section 3 (Technology & Product) is now the weakest: its patent table is mostly 'not verified' and no blocking patent family is established.
answers.unpriced_risk: The AI cost curve. The base case holds a 33% operating margin and treats the Gemini licence as a roughly $1bn R&D expense, but R&D is already up 33% to $34.04bn with no disclosed AI revenue (section 6, S6), and the scenario analysis gives the licence only a low-confidence assumption with no number attached. A per-device or per-query price across the 2.5bn installed base would be several times $1bn and would land in the 76.3% services margin, a 2-4% EPS risk that the $270 entry and the 1.5-2.0% starter size do not adjust for. The same gap covers the xAI suit against Apple over AI distribution, which no section prices.
answers.first_challenge: Why own nothing at 35.2x forward when the franchise compounds at 8-11% and the buyback adds 2.4 points of EPS growth? The answer has to be the exit multiple, not the business: section 12 shows a 1.3% three-year return from $344.63 if the multiple reverts to the 31.0x mean (S97). A partner would immediately challenge the $270 entry as arbitrary, because it is derived from a required 9% return rather than from the franchise: at 29x the scenario base gives $284, so $270 is a 5% discount to the base case, not a margin of safety, and it is above the $241 bear case.
answers.downside_survival: The recommendation survives; the entry price does not. A market 50% smaller takes group revenue down about 35% and EPS to roughly $6, which at 20-25x is $120-150, but $62.2bn of net cash means the company survives and the buyback stops rather than the balance sheet breaking. Revenue 30% lower gives operating income of about $95bn and EPS of $5.4; the bottom of the DCF range is $133 at a 9.5% cost of equity and a 30% margin, and the exit-multiple bear is $241 at 24.6x. Free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn on the $122.6-127.3bn band (central $125.1bn, 0.97x conversion), 56.4-58.6x on the $5,029.6bn market value, which covers the $82.2bn trailing buyback but not $97.9bn of trailing buybacks and dividends; the deferred-consideration case at $123.2bn changes neither, and the $111.5bn reading is withdrawn because the $13,531M non-current build fits inside the $10,016M other-liabilities line once the $4,128M fall in other current liabilities is netted. Net cash absorbs three or more years of the gap. CAC doubling and a six-month financing delay do not apply (no customer acquisition cost; net cash and $12.4bn due within a year), so the analogues are a licence doubling to $2bn, about 1.3% of operating income, and a buyback pause, -2.4 points of EPS growth. Multiple compression from 35.2x forward to 24.6x is -30.1%.
answers.ocr_claims: There are no OCR-derived claims in the report. Every figure in section 10 and in the review comes from an SEC filing, a market-data feed, a named research firm's release or a cited publication, and no client document was read through OCR in this run.

user_data_requests.database: PACER — U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey, docket for United States v. Apple Inc., No. 2:24-cv-04055
user_data_requests.query: Docket entries and orders after June 2025: the ruling on Apple's motion to dismiss, the current scheduling order and trial date, and any order defining the remedy theories that remain in the case.
user_data_requests.why: The timing and scope of a US remedy against App Store and device-interoperability rules are the largest long-dated regulatory tail in the investment case; Apple's filings disclose the case but not the schedule or which claims survived dismissal.
user_data_requests.how: Log in to PACER, open the D.N.J. docket 2:24-cv-04055, download the docket sheet and the motion-to-dismiss and scheduling orders, and attach them.

user_data_requests.database: European Commission DMA case register — DMA.100206 (Apple new business terms) and the Article 6(4) non-compliance proceeding
user_data_requests.query: Any formal decision, commitment decision or closure of the Article 6(4) and Article 5(4) proceedings accepting Apple's 18 August 2026 EU business terms; the non-confidential decision text and the effective fee schedule.
user_data_requests.why: It determines whether the 26%/20%/15%/5% EU fee schedule is a binding settlement or an interim step, and therefore whether EU App Store take-rate erosion is settled or still exposed to further Commission action and fines.
user_data_requests.how: Search the Commission's DMA case register for DMA.100206 and the Apple non-compliance cases, download the latest decision and press release, and attach them.

user_data_requests.database: IDC Worldwide Quarterly Mobile Phone Tracker (regional pivot) or Canalys/Omdia regional smartphone dataset — paid subscription
user_data_requests.query: Smartphone market value in USD and unit shipments by region (Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, Rest of Asia-Pacific) for 2023-2026, with the premium segment (wholesale ASP $600+) split by vendor.
user_data_requests.why: Free releases give global market value ($613B for 2026) and China units only. Without the regional pivot I cannot size the regional TAM or compute Apple's share of each regional market, so the regional growth table relies on Apple's own segment revenue as a proxy and the durability conclusion is weaker for Americas, Europe, Japan and Rest of Asia-Pacific.
user_data_requests.how: Export the regional market-value pivot from the IDC tracker (or the equivalent Canalys/Omdia workbook) and attach the Excel or PDF to the case file.

user_data_requests.database: PACER — US v. Google LLC, D.D.C. No. 1:20-cv-03010 (remedies record and trial exhibits on the Apple default-search agreement)
user_data_requests.query: The current Apple–Google Safari default-search agreement terms: the revenue share (36% of Safari search advertising in the 2022 record), the annual amount paid to Apple for the most recent year, and the renewal/termination terms under Judge Mehta's 2025-12-05 final judgment.
user_data_requests.why: Apple discloses no search-licensing revenue. The only public figure is the 2022 payment of $20B, which is 16.6% of trailing-twelve-month services revenue and 12.9% of operating income. Whether the 2026 run-rate is $20B or $30B changes the size of the largest single repricing risk in the business model section by half.
user_data_requests.how: Download the final judgment and the revenue-share exhibits from the D.D.C. docket on PACER (fee per page), or use the Department of Justice antitrust division's public case page for US v. Google, which posts the opinions and trial exhibits without a login.

user_data_requests.database: USPTO Patent Center and PatentsView (patent search and grant counts)
user_data_requests.query: For Apple Inc. (assignee): granted and pending US patents filed 2023-2026 in foldable hinges/displays, on-device model compression and optical health sensing, with patent numbers, filing and grant dates and status; plus Apple's US grant count for 2025 and 2026.
user_data_requests.why: The technology section's patent table rests on an aggregate grant count (2,722 in 2025, down 12%) and could not cite a single verified patent number or a granted-versus-pending mix. Without it, freedom-to-operate risk in foldable hinges and health sensing cannot be assessed, which is the one part of the moat argument left at low confidence.
user_data_requests.how: PatentsView's current API needs a key (free registration at search.patentsview.org); alternatively export a Patent Center search by assignee "Apple Inc." for CPC codes on hinges (E05D), displays and PPG sensing, 2023-2026, as CSV.

user_data_requests.database: Apple Investor Relations leadership and governance biographies (investor.apple.com/leadership-and-governance and apple.com/leadership)
user_data_requests.query: Degrees, prior employers and start dates for Craig Federighi, Eddy Cue, Johny Srouji, Sabih Khan, Kevan Parekh, Deirdre O'Brien, Jennifer Newstead, Amar Subramanya and John Ternus.
user_data_requests.why: Apple's proxy discloses no university degrees for any named executive and no pay or ownership for its technology leaders, so six of seven executive education cells and the prior-career records of the AI, software and silicon leaders cannot be verified from filings. Filling them determines whether the bench really has AI and cloud depth, which is the core of the team judgement.
user_data_requests.how: Open investor.apple.com/leadership-and-governance, open each executive's bio, and save the pages as PDF or paste the bio text (about 12 profiles).

user_data_requests.database: Bloomberg, FactSet or LSEG consensus (subscription terminal)
user_data_requests.query: AAPL consensus revenue, EPS and free cash flow for FY2027 and FY2028, the consensus 12-month price target, and trailing/forward P/E and EV/EBIT for Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and Xiaomi (1810.HK) as of 2026-10-30
user_data_requests.why: The valuation section states Apple's forward consensus as "not disclosed" because no free source in this run carried it, and the two named global handset peers could not be valued at all: they file no US GAAP accounts. Without the estimates the DCF's 9%-to-5% growth fade cannot be checked against the street, and the peer premium is measured against US platform names only, which understates or overstates Apple's premium depending on Samsung's and Xiaomi's multiples.
user_data_requests.how: Export the consensus summary page (revenue, EPS, FCF, target price) for AAPL and the valuation multiples screen for 005930.KS and 1810.HK, dated 2026-10-30, as a PDF or spreadsheet.

esg.markdown:
Apple's regulatory exposure, not its ESG record, is what can change a long-only case. FY2025 net sales were $416.2bn and Services revenue $109.2bn at a 75.4% gross margin, so App Store commissions and the Google default-search payment sit inside the profit pool carrying the premium multiple [S5]. Fines are not the mechanism; remedies and fee schedules are. The bear case is a 10-15% operating-income tail from losing or repricing search placement and a structurally lower App Store take rate over 2026-2028.

### The EU fine is small; the fee schedule is not

On 2025-04-23 the European Commission fined Apple €500m for breaching the DMA anti-steering obligation, 0.1% of FY2025 net sales. The material part is the fee schedule: from 2026-10-01 Apple's unified EU terms charge 26% on in-app purchase (down from 30%), 20% on alternative payment processing, 15% on link-outs and 5% on apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web. Apple says the terms resolve its disagreements with the Commission; EU developer groups call them unacceptable, so the settlement is contested. The General Court dismissed Apple's challenge to its gatekeeper designation on 2026-07-08, with an interoperability ruling unlikely before late 2027. Apple does not disclose EU App Store revenue; at a 75.4% Services margin, each $1bn of commission lost equals about $0.75bn of gross profit [S78, S77, S82, S5].

### The $20 billion Google payment is the largest policy-sensitive cash flow

Apple does not disclose the Google default-search payment, but the US v. Google trial record put it at about $20bn in 2022, or 36% of Google's Safari search revenue: a litigated estimate, not a company disclosure. That is 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue and, if near-pure margin, about 15% of operating income. Judge Mehta's final judgment of 2025-12-05 preserved non-exclusive payments, banned exclusivity and capped default deals at 12 months; the DOJ and states cross-appealed in February 2026 seeking a payment ban. A negotiated lower rate is more likely than zero, but either compresses Services growth, and an appellate decision is likely in 2027 [S80, S76, S5].

### US courts are already narrowing the App Store take rate

The US threat is not hypothetical. On 2025-12-11 the Ninth Circuit affirmed that Apple willfully violated the Epic injunction, upheld the steering remedy and limited any fee on linked transactions to Apple's costs; the Supreme Court granted certiorari on 2026-06-30. Separately, the DOJ and 16 states and DC have sued Apple for monopolization in "performance smartphones" and "smartphones" since 2024-03-21, seeking equitable relief, not damages; the case is in pre-trial litigation with no trial date in Apple's 2026 filings. A federal appellate court finding willful violation raises the odds of stricter remedies and weakens management's "substantial defenses" posture [S79, S81, S6].

### Tariffs have flipped from cost to refund, not to a new margin level

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $109.4bn and gross margin 50.1%, including 2 percentage points from tariff refunds; EPS of $2.02 included $0.11 from refunds. The underlying margin is about 48.1%, against 46.9% for FY2025, when products gross margin fell on tariff costs. The refund follows the Supreme Court's 2026-02-20 ruling striking down certain IEEPA tariffs; Section 232 semiconductor initial results on 2026-01-14 imposed no additional tariffs on Apple products, but Section 301 duties have since been imposed and further actions remain possible. Underwrite 47-48%, not 50% [S17, S5, S6].

### Governance is a strength; the ESG gaps are disclosure and labour

Governance is not the discount. Apple has eight directors, three of them women (37.5%), an independent chair separate from the CEO, no dual-class stock, a $120,000 related-party review threshold, Audit Committee ownership of privacy and cybersecurity, and 92% Say-on-Pay support in 2025. The gaps are supply-chain labour and disclosure: about 166,000 employees at 2025-09-27, a 10-K concession that supplier code violations "occur from time to time", and no audit metrics in the filing. Climate and carbon-neutrality statements are company claims not independently verified here; none has changed demand, so they matter through legal and reputational tail, not near-term cash flow [S11, S5].

esg.author: Regulatory Analyst
esg.markdown:
Apple's regulatory exposure, not its ESG record, is what can change a long-only case. FY2025 net sales were $416.2bn and Services revenue $109.2bn at a 75.4% gross margin, so App Store commissions and the Google default-search payment sit inside the profit pool carrying the premium multiple [S5]. Fines are not the mechanism; remedies and fee schedules are. Bear case: a 10-15% operating-income tail from losing or repricing search placement and a structurally lower App Store take rate over 2026-2028. A dollar of commission or default rent carries almost no marginal cost, so losing it hits operating income faster than revenue.

### The EU fine is small; the fee schedule is not

On 2025-04-23 the European Commission fined Apple €500m for breaching the DMA anti-steering obligation, 0.1% of FY2025 net sales. The material part is the fee schedule: from 2026-10-01 Apple's unified EU terms charge 26% on in-app purchase (down from 30%), 20% on alternative payments, 15% on link-outs and 5% on apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web. Apple calls the terms a settlement; EU developer groups contest them. Apple does not disclose EU App Store revenue; at a 75.4% Services margin, each $1bn of commission lost equals $0.75bn of gross profit, and the take rate falls permanently [S78, S77, S5].

### The $20 billion Google payment is the largest policy-sensitive cash flow

Apple does not disclose the Google default-search payment, but the US v. Google trial record put it at $20bn in 2022, or 36% of Google's Safari search revenue: a litigated estimate, not an Apple disclosure. That is 18.3% of FY2025 Services revenue and, if near-pure margin, 15% of operating income. Judge Mehta's final judgment of 2025-12-05 preserved non-exclusive payments, banned exclusivity and capped default deals at 12 months; the DOJ and states cross-appealed in February 2026 seeking a payment ban. A lower negotiated rate is more likely than zero, because the payment is worth more as Apple profit than as Google cost; either way it compresses Services growth, and an appellate decision is likely in 2027 [S80, S76, S5].

### US courts are already narrowing the App Store take rate

On 2025-12-11 the Ninth Circuit affirmed that Apple willfully violated the Epic injunction, upheld the steering remedy and limited any fee on linked transactions to Apple's costs; the Supreme Court granted certiorari on 2026-06-30. The DOJ and 16 states and DC have sued Apple for monopolization of "performance smartphones" and "smartphones" since 2024-03-21, seeking equitable relief, not damages; pre-trial litigation has no trial date in Apple's 2026 filings. A willful-violation finding raises the odds of stricter remedies and weakens management's "substantial defenses" posture. US courts can reset App Store economics before the DOJ case reaches trial [S79, S81, S6].

### Tariffs have flipped from cost to refund, not to a new margin level

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $109.4bn and gross margin 50.1%, including 2 percentage points from tariff refunds; EPS of $2.02 included $0.11 from refunds. The underlying margin is 48.1%, against 46.9% for FY2025, when products gross margin fell on tariff costs. The refund follows the Supreme Court's 2026-02-20 ruling striking down certain IEEPA tariffs; Section 232 semiconductor results on 2026-01-14 imposed no additional tariffs on Apple products, but Section 301 duties have since been imposed and more remain possible. For valuation, normalise the margin rather than extrapolate the refund: underwrite 47-48%, not 50% [S17, S5, S6].

### Governance is sound, but the chair is now the former CEO

Governance is not the discount, but the structure changed on 2026-09-01: Tim Cook became Executive Chair, John Ternus became CEO and a ninth director, and Arthur Levinson became Lead Independent Director. The chair is the former CEO, not independent; the independent check now rests on the lead director. The board also waived its guideline against re-election after age 75 for Levinson (75) and Audit Chair Ron Sugar (77), both re-elected in 2026, so refreshment lags the rule. Offsetting that, there is no dual-class stock, four of the 2026 directors were women, the Audit Committee owns privacy and cybersecurity, related-party transactions above $120,000 need its approval, and the 2026 executive-pay vote passed. The gaps are labour and disclosure: 166,000 employees at 2025-09-27, a 10-K concession that supplier code violations "occur from time to time", and no audit metrics; climate claims are unverified. None has changed demand, so ESG is a tail-risk and discount-rate input, not a revenue driver [S56, S11, S138].

business_model.author: Fundamentals Analyst
business_model.markdown:
Apple monetises the same customer twice: once through a hardware sale at a 39.9% gross margin that is paid for before the cost is incurred, and again through a services annuity at a 76.3% gross margin that costs almost nothing incremental to serve. Over the twelve months to 27 June 2026 the company recorded $466,823M of revenue and $227,123M of gross profit — iPhone $245,540M (52.6% of revenue), Services $120,478M (25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit), Mac $35,863M, Wearables, Home and Accessories $36,290M and iPad $28,652M. Services gross profit of $91,607M covers total company R&D of $42,901M 2.1 times, so the annuity already pays for the AI build-out. The mix, not the growth rate, is what an investor is underwriting. [S5, S6]

### The 2026 acceleration is hardware, not annuity

In the nine months to 27 June 2026 revenue grew 16.1%, but the engines ran at different speeds: iPhone +22.4%, Mac +8.6%, iPad +3.0%, Wearables +2.3%, Services +14.1%. Services therefore fell to 25.2% of revenue from 26.2% in FY2025 — the first year-over-year decline in the mix since at least FY2023, when services were 22.2% of revenue. Greater China grew 30% after shrinking 4% in FY2025. The standard account of Apple as a services compounder is not what the last three quarters show; they show an iPhone cycle carried by Pro-model mix, with the annuity growing at roughly half the pace. The counterpoint is that 14.1% growth on a $109,158M FY2025 base is about $15B of incremental annual revenue at a 76% margin, which is more gross profit than most software companies generate in total. [S5, S6]

### What one device earns

Apple stopped disclosing unit shipments, so the most defensible unit is the active device. On the 2.5 billion active devices the company cited in January 2026 — a statement made on an earnings call, not a filed figure — the trailing-twelve-month flows divide as follows.

| Per active device, per year | Amount | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $186.7 | $466,823M TTM ÷ 2.5bn devices | S6, S73 |
| of which Services | $48.2 | $120,478M TTM ÷ 2.5bn | S6, S73 |
| Gross profit | $90.8 | 48.7% blended gross margin | S6 |
| Selling, general and administrative | ($11.7) | $29,363M TTM | S6 |
| Research and development | ($17.2) | $42,901M TTM | S6 |
| Operating profit | $61.9 | $154,859M TTM | S6 |
| Gross profit ÷ selling cost | 7.8x a year | $90.8 ÷ $11.7 | S6 |
| Cash payback on acquisition | immediate | cash conversion cycle −56.8 days | S5, S6 |

The waterfall ends where most hardware businesses begin: there is no customer-acquisition payback period to compute, because Apple is paid by carriers and retailers before it pays its assemblers. Payables of $64,525M against inventory of $11,092M produced a cash conversion cycle of −56.8 days at 27 June 2026, against +39.2 days at Alphabet; each new device is cash-positive on day one. That advantage is not a scale economy a rival can buy with capital — it is the accounting consequence of owning the customer and outsourcing the factory. [S6, S73]

### The annuity rests on two contested tolls

The 10-K describes Services as advertising (including third-party licensing arrangements), AppleCare, cloud, the App Store, subscription content and payment services, but never splits their revenue. Two of those lines are tolls on other people's commerce. The first is the App Store commission of 15-30%: on 11 December 2025 the Ninth Circuit held that Apple's 27% commission on purchases made after a user follows a link out of an app had a prohibitive effect, and remanded for the district court to decide what commission, if any, may be charged. The second is the Google default-search licence, where court records show Apple received 36% of search advertising revenue generated through Safari and about $20B in 2022 — roughly 17% of trailing services revenue and 13% of operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy kept the payments but barred exclusivity and capped any default arrangement at twelve months, and Google appealed on 22 May 2026. [S69, S70]

| Offer | Price or take rate | Margin or peer benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone (upfront hardware) | implied ASP ≈ $941 ($245,540M TTM ÷ 261M estimated units) | products gross margin 39.9% | S6, S74 |
| App Store (commission) | 15-30%; the 27% link-out commission was ruled prohibitive | services gross margin 76.3% | S6, S69 |
| Safari default search | 36% of Safari search advertising; ≈$20B paid in 2022 | ≈17% of TTM services revenue | S70 |
| Subscriptions and cloud | recurring, bundled at the device sale | services 76.3% vs Microsoft 67.9% in FY2026 | S6, S49 |
| Handset peer — Samsung devices (DX) | — | KRW 0.8tn operating loss in Q3 2026 | S75 |

### The cost side has turned

The 2026 margin record is partly purchased. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9% a year earlier, and the 10-Q attributes the gain to product mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by higher costs including memory; the third-quarter release put the refund benefit at about 2 percentage points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS. Against that, memory prices rose about 146% in the first quarter of 2026 versus the 2025 average, and Samsung's own mobile memory costs more than doubled. Apple's filing expects the component trends "to intensify, which may materially negatively impact" revenue, costs and gross margin, and concedes that price increases "may also reduce demand" — the elasticity admission a hardware model has to make. A 47-48% gross margin is the defensible base case, not the 50.1% just printed. [S17, S68]

### What this means for the watchlist

The business is a negative-working-capital hardware engine bolted to a high-margin annuity, and the annuity is the terminal value. That structure justifies a premium to hardware peers but not a software multiple on the whole revenue base, because a quarter of revenue sits in a line where two tolls are being repriced in court, and a large slice of the rest faces a memory cycle that turns faster than Apple can re-price handsets. At $344.63 on 30 October 2026 the market capitalisation is about $5.07T, or 39x trailing EPS of $8.72; the price already assumes the annuity survives intact and that memory costs are passed through. The conditions that would make a long actionable are specific: services growth re-accelerating above 15% without hardware mix, a remand ruling that preserves a mid-teens link-out take rate, and a memory cost peak visible in supplier guidance. Confidence in the mix arithmetic is high because it comes from filed segment data; confidence in the durability of the tolls is medium, because Apple discloses neither their size nor their terms.

::: evidence
**The services annuity is what the multiple buys, and it is a smaller share of revenue than it was a year ago.**

Services produced $120,478M of trailing-twelve-month revenue — 25.8% of the total but 40.3% of gross profit and 2.1x company R&D — while its revenue share fell to 25.2% in the nine months to 27 June 2026 as iPhone revenue grew 22.4% against services growth of 14.1% (S5, S6, S17). Two tolls inside that line, the App Store commission and the Safari search licence worth about 17% of services revenue on a 2022 court figure, are both under active legal challenge (S69, S70).
:::

business_model.author: Fundamentals Analyst
business_model.markdown:
Apple monetises the same customer twice: once through a hardware sale at a 39.9% gross margin that is paid for before the cost is incurred, and again through a services annuity at a 76.3% gross margin that costs almost nothing incremental to serve. Over the twelve months to 27 June 2026 the company recorded $466,823M of revenue and $227,123M of gross profit — iPhone $245,540M (52.6% of revenue), Services $120,478M (25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit), Mac $35,863M, Wearables, Home and Accessories $36,290M and iPad $28,652M. Services gross profit of $91,607M covers total company R&D of $42,901M 2.1 times, so the annuity already pays for the AI build-out. The mix, not the growth rate, is what an investor is underwriting. [S5, S6]

### The 2026 acceleration is hardware, not annuity

In the nine months to 27 June 2026 revenue grew 16.1%, but the engines ran at different speeds: iPhone +22.4%, Mac +8.6%, iPad +3.0%, Wearables +2.3%, Services +14.1%. Services therefore fell to 25.2% of revenue from 26.2% in FY2025 — the first year-over-year decline in the mix since at least FY2023, when services were 22.2% of revenue. Greater China grew 30% after shrinking 4% in FY2025. The standard account of Apple as a services compounder is not what the last three quarters show; they show an iPhone cycle carried by Pro-model mix, with the annuity growing at 14.1% against iPhone's 22.4%. The counterpoint is that 14.1% growth on a $109,158M FY2025 base is $15,391M of incremental annual revenue at a 76.3% margin, more gross profit than most software companies generate in total. [S5, S6]

### What one device earns

Apple stopped disclosing unit shipments, so the most defensible unit is the active device. The table divides trailing-twelve-month flows by Apple's own installed-base statement; because that base is an earnings-call figure rather than a filed one, every line is an estimate.

| Line item | Per unit — per active device, per year | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $186.7 | $466,823M TTM ÷ 2,500M devices | S6, S73 |
| of which Services | $48.2 | $120,478M TTM ÷ 2,500M | S6, S73 |
| Gross profit | $90.8 | 48.7% blended gross margin | S6 |
| Selling, general and administrative | ($11.7) | $29,363M TTM | S6 |
| Research and development | ($17.2) | $42,901M TTM | S6 |
| Operating profit | $61.9 | $154,859M TTM | S6 |
| Gross profit ÷ selling cost | 7.8x a year | $90.8 ÷ $11.7 | S6 |
| Cash payback on acquisition | immediate | cash conversion cycle −56.8 days | S5, S6 |

The waterfall ends where most hardware businesses begin: there is no customer-acquisition payback period to compute, because Apple is paid by carriers and retailers before it pays its assemblers. Payables of $64,525M against inventory of $11,092M produced a cash conversion cycle of −56.8 days at 27 June 2026, against +39.2 days at Alphabet; each new device is cash-positive on day one. That advantage is not a scale economy a rival can buy with capital — it is the accounting consequence of owning the customer and outsourcing the factory. [S6, S73]

### The annuity rests on two contested tolls

The 10-K describes Services as advertising (including third-party licensing arrangements), AppleCare, cloud, the App Store, subscription content and payment services, but never splits their revenue. Two of those lines are tolls on other people's commerce. The first is the App Store commission: on 11 December 2025 the Ninth Circuit held that Apple's 27% commission on purchases made after a user follows a link out of an app had a prohibitive effect, and remanded for the district court to decide what commission, if any, may be charged. The second is the Google default-search licence, where court records show Apple received 36% of search advertising revenue generated through Safari and a 2022 payment put at $20B — 16.6% of trailing-twelve-month services revenue of $120,478M and 12.9% of trailing-twelve-month operating income of $154,859M; measured on FY2025 the same $20B would be 18.3% of $109,158M services revenue and 15.0% of $133,050M operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy kept the payments but barred exclusivity and capped any default arrangement at twelve months, and Google's D.C. Circuit brief of 22 May 2026 challenges that judgment. [S69, S70]

|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone (upfront hardware) | implied ASP $941 ($245,540M TTM ÷ 261M estimated units) | products gross margin 39.9% | S6, S74 |
| App Store (commission, ex-EU) | 15-30%; the 27% link-out commission was ruled prohibitive | services gross margin 76.3% | S6, S69 |
| App Store (EU, from 2026-10-01) | 26% in-app purchase, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission | EU band 5-26% against 15-30% elsewhere | S77, S78 |
| Safari default search | 36% of Safari search advertising; $20B in 2022 | 16.6% of TTM services revenue | S70 |
| Subscriptions and cloud | recurring, bundled at the device sale | services 76.3% vs Microsoft 67.9% in FY2026 | S6, S49 |
| Handset peer — Samsung devices (DX) | — | KRW 0.8tn operating loss in Q3 2026 | S75 |

### The cost side has turned

The 2026 margin record is partly purchased. market.author: Market Analyst
market.markdown:
Apple's markets are large but no longer volume-growth markets: the smartphone unit pool is contracting at the fastest rate on record in 2026 while its dollar value rises, so revenue growth to 2030 must come from holding more than 40% of smartphone value, monetising a record installed base through services, and a foldable and AI-driven upgrade cycle, not from market growth. Apple's revenue compounded at 3.3% from FY2021 to FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and then accelerated to 16% in the first nine months of FY2026, with iPhone revenue up 22% [S5, S6].

| Measure | Figure | Period | Method and note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global smartphone units | 1.26B | 2025 | Counterpoint full year, +2% YoY; Omdia 1.25B (+2%) | S92 |
| Global smartphone units | just over 1.0B | 2026E | IDC, -16.7% YoY, steepest annual fall on record | S84 |
| Global smartphone market value | $613B | 2026E | IDC, +6.3% YoY | S84 |
| Global smartphone ASP | $581 | 2026E | IDC, +27.6%; Omdia independently $565 (+21%) | S84, S88 |
| Premium segment (wholesale ASP $600+) | 29% of global units | H1 2026 | Counterpoint; 25% in H1 2025, 20% in H1 2022 | S94 |
| Apple iPhone revenue | $209.6B FY2025; $196.5B 9M FY2026 | FY2025 / 9M FY2026 | Apple filings; +22% in 9M FY2026 | S5, S6 |
| Apple share of smartphone value | 36% FY2025; 42.7% annualised 2026 | FY2025 / 2026 | Calculated: iPhone revenue / (units x ASP); 2026 = $196.5B x 4/3 / $613B | S5, S6, S92, S88 |
| Wearables units | 625M | 2026E | IDC, +1.7%; 2.4% CAGR to 687M by 2030 | S85 |
| Global advertising pool (services) | $1.34T | 2026E | WARC, +11.9% | S89 |

Two independent methods agree that the market is growing in dollars while shrinking in units. Top-down, IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0B units, down 16.7%, while total market value rises 6.3% to $613B because average selling prices jump 27.6% to $581; Omdia independently forecasts ASP rising from $467 in 2025 to $565 in 2026, a 21% increase it calls the largest on record [S84, S88]. Bottom-up, 1.0B units at $581 imply $581B, within 5% of IDC's value line, so the two methods reconcile on direction and approximate size. The mechanism is a memory cost shock, with NAND and DRAM prices up more than 300% year over year, passed through to shelf prices. The market is not expanding; it is being repriced, and the vendors with premium mix and supply leverage capture the difference.

Apple's revenue sits where the market is concentrating. Premium handsets reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026, up from 25% a year earlier and 20% in H1 2022, and Apple took 65% of those premium units with 9% growth [S94, S92, S84, S5, S6, S88]. Its all-vendor unit share was 20% in 2025, and IDC expects iOS share to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android shipments fall 24.3%. On my calculation Apple captured 36% of global smartphone value in FY2025, $209.6B of iPhone revenue against a $588B market at 1.26B units and a $467 ASP, and annualising nine-month FY2026 iPhone revenue gives $262B, or 42.7% of IDC's $613B 2026 value. Value capture, not unit share, is the franchise an investor is buying.

The durability test is whether that value capture survives a 20-30% price increase, and the evidence is mixed. Apple's product gross margin rose to 40.1% in Q3 FY2026 from 34.5% a year earlier on richer mix and tariff refunds, and revenue grew in every geographic segment in double digits; that is genuine pricing power [S17, S87, S84]. But IDC attributes part of the China strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half price increases, and warns China's decline could widen to 20% in H2 2026. The sub-$100 segment, 173M units in 2025, fell nearly 60% in Q2 2026 and emerging markets are forecast down more than 20%. A market that grows in dollars while shrinking in units can flatter Apple for four to six quarters and then mean-revert; the base rate is the 3.3% revenue CAGR of FY2021-FY2025, not the 16% of the last nine months.

Three pools can add revenue to 2030, and only one is large enough to change the trajectory [S84, S6, S83, S89, S85, S95]. Foldables: Apple enters in H2 2026, and IDC expects it to ship more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, about 40% of a category worth more than $45.7B. Services: $120.5B on a trailing-twelve-month basis to June 2026, growing 14.1% in nine months at a 76.3% gross margin, against a global advertising pool of $1.34T in 2026 and an App Store ecosystem Apple says carried $149B of digital goods and services in 2025. Wearables and PC: wearables are a 2.4% CAGR market to 2030 with smartwatches shrinking 3.7% in 2026 while glasses grow 18.1% a year, and the Mac gained share to 9.9% in a PC market down 4.9%. Foldables and services can add; the non-phone device pools, $33.7B of Mac and $35.7B of wearables in FY2025, are too small to carry group growth alone.

| Region | Market size (latest dated) | Growth | Company's position | Barriers | Key competitors | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Americas | Global pool $613B (2026E); regional value not published in free trackers | Apple +11.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; home market; 42.9% of FY2025 revenue | US tariffs (Section 232 and 301); platform antitrust | Samsung, Google, Motorola | S84, S5, S6 |
| Europe | Not published | Apple +16.1% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 26.7% of revenue | DMA take-rate cuts from 2026-10-01; GDPR | Samsung, Xiaomi, Google | S77, S6 |
| Greater China | 66M units in Q2 2026; 134M in H1 2026 | Market -4.3% in Q2 2026; H2 2026 decline could reach 20%; Apple +30.0% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 18.1% share versus Huawei 22.6% | Market access; local champion; data rules | Huawei, OPPO, vivo, Xiaomi, Honor | S87, S6 |
| Japan | Not published | Apple +10.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 6.9% of revenue | Yen weakness; carrier-controlled channel | Samsung, Google, Sharp | S6 |
| Rest of Asia-Pacific | Not published; emerging markets forecast down more than 20% in 2026 | Apple +19.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 8.1% of revenue; India manufacturing and retail expansion | Price sensitivity; tariffs | Samsung, Xiaomi, vivo, OPPO, Transsion | S84, S6 |

Geography splits the durability question, and policy is a live variable in every region [S6, S87, S77]. Greater China is 15.5% of revenue but produced 30% growth in the first nine months of FY2026; Europe is 26.7% and grew 16%, the Americas 42.9% and 11%, Japan 6.9% and 10%, and Rest of Asia-Pacific 8.1% and 19%. The China number is the most fragile: the market fell 4.3% in Q2 2026, Apple's 18.1% share trailed Huawei's 22.6%, and the top six vendors hold 96%. The EU's DMA terms cut the commission on externally distributed digital transactions to 5% from 1 October 2026; US tariffs moved twice in 2026, with the Supreme Court striking down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026 and Section 301 duties imposed since, while the Section 232 semiconductor review produced no additional tariffs on Apple products on 14 January 2026. Demand is overwhelmingly organic consumer replacement rather than policy-created: China's subsidy support faded in 2026 and India's incentives are supply-side manufacturing support, not consumer demand. The budget owner is the consumer or the carrier financing plan, the procurement cycle follows the annual September launch, and willingness to pay is being tested by a 27.6% market ASP increase. What would change the conclusion is services growth above 15% with user growth, a foldable cycle that adds the $45.7B category value IDC projects, or China stabilising after the H2 2026 air pocket. Confidence is high on 2026 data and low on 2027-2030 regional sizing, because regional market values are paywalled and Apple does not disclose units; the open questions are what share of iPhone growth is units versus price, whether services growth is users or price, how much China demand was pulled forward, and how much memory cost Apple can pass through in FY2027.

::: evidence
**Apple's markets are growing in dollars while shrinking in units, so its growth is price- and share-led, not market-led.**

The global pool is $613B of smartphone value in 2026 against just over 1.0B units, with a 27.6% ASP increase doing the work volume used to do (IDC, S84). Premium concentration (29% of units) and Apple's 65% share of it explain why Apple captures 36-43% of value on 20-24% of units (Counterpoint, S94; Apple filings, S5, S6). Foldables ($45.7B of category value by 2027) and services ($120.5B TTM at 76.3% gross margin) are the only pools large enough to move group growth; wearables grow 2.4% a year to 2030 (IDC, S85).
:::

Two independent methods agree that the market is growing in dollars while shrinking in units, and the sizing stacks into three layers. TAM: top-down, IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0B units, down 16.7%, while total market value rises 6.3% to $613B because average selling prices jump 27.6% to $581; Omdia independently forecasts ASP rising from $467 in 2025 to $565 in 2026, a 21% increase it calls the largest on record [S84, S88]. SOM: Apple's current capture, $466.8B of trailing-twelve-month revenue to June 2026, of which $245.5B is iPhone and $120.5B services. Bottom-up, 1.0B units at $581 imply $581B, within 5% of IDC's value line. The mechanism is a memory cost shock: IDC puts NAND and DRAM costs more than 300% above a year earlier, and the increase is passed through to shelf prices; the market is not expanding, it is being repriced.

Apple's revenue sits where the market is concentrating. Premium handsets reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026, up from 25% a year earlier and 20% in H1 2022, and Apple took 65% of those premium units with 9% growth [S94, S92, S84, S5, S6, S88]. Its all-vendor unit share was 20% in 2025, and IDC expects iOS share to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android shipments fall 24.3%. On my calculation Apple captured 36% of global smartphone value in FY2025, $209.6B of iPhone revenue against a $588B market at 1.26B units and a $467 ASP, and annualising nine-month FY2026 iPhone revenue gives $262B, or 42.7% of IDC's $613B 2026 value. Apple's product gross margin rose to 40.1% in Q3 FY2026 from 34.5% a year earlier on richer mix and tariff refunds, and revenue grew in every geographic segment in double digits; that is genuine pricing power [S17, S87, S84]. But IDC attributes part of the China strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half price increases, and warns China's decline could widen to 20% in H2 2026. The sub-$100 segment, 173M units in 2025, fell nearly 60% in Q2 2026 and emerging markets are forecast down more than 20%. Foldables: Apple enters in H2 2026, and IDC expects it to ship more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, 40% of a category worth more than $45.7B. Geography splits the durability question, and policy is a live variable in every region [S6, S87, S77]. ::: evidence
**Apple's markets are growing in dollars while shrinking in units, so its growth is price- and share-led, not market-led.**

The global pool is $613B of smartphone value in 2026 against just over 1.0B units, with a 27.6% ASP increase doing the work volume used to do (IDC, S84). :::

financials.author: Fundamentals Analyst
financials.markdown:
Apple's profit is unusually cash-true. Over the twelve months to 27 June 2026 operating cash flow was $146,724M, capital expenditure $10,041M and free cash flow $136,683M against net income of $128,930M — conversion of 1.06x on capex of 2.2% of revenue, against 0.50x and 39.2% at Microsoft and 0.08x and 33.9% at Alphabet. The income statement behind that cash grew revenue from $383,285M in FY2023 to $416,161M in FY2025 and $466,823M trailing, with operating margin of 29.8%, 32.0% and 33.2%. The nine months to 27 June 2026 produced an incremental operating margin of 43.0% — $21,809M more operating income on $50,662M more revenue — which is the bull case in one line. The question is how much of that increment is repeatable. [S5, S6]

| Ten-year Treasury yield, 30 October 2026 | 4.93% | — | — | S10 |

### The margin is the record, and part of it was purchased

Gross margin went from 44.1% in FY2023 to 46.2%, 46.9%, 49.1% in the nine months of FY2026 and 48.7% trailing, and the June 2026 quarter printed 50.1%, the highest Apple has reported. Part of that is structural: services, at a 76.3% gross margin, are 40.3% of the gross-profit pool on 25.8% of revenue. Part is not. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9% on product mix and tariff refunds, and the 30 July 2026 release attributes 2 percentage points of the quarter's gross margin and $0.11 of its $2.02 EPS to those refunds. The cost side has turned: memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 against the 2025 average, Samsung's mobile memory costs rose 107%, and the 10-Q expects the component trends "to intensify". A 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1%, is the level to capitalise. [S17, S68]

::: info warning
**Two percentage points of the record 50.1% gross margin are a one-off tariff refund, and the memory cycle is turning against the hardware line.**

The 30 July 2026 release puts the refund at 2 points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 quarterly EPS (S17); nine-month products gross margin of 39.9% compares with 36.9% a year earlier on mix and refunds, while memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 and Apple's 10-Q warns cost pressure will intensify (S6, S68). Two hundred basis points off the trailing gross margin is $0.52 of EPS, or 6.0% of the $8.72.
:::

### Cash conversion is real; the 2026 step-up is partly working capital

Nine-month operating cash flow rose 43.1% to $116,996M while net income rose 20.0%, and the balance sheet shows why: receivables fell to $31,398M from $39,777M and vendor non-trade receivables to $27,509M from $33,180M, cutting days sales outstanding to 24.5 from 34.9, while inventory rose to $11,092M from $5,718M and payables fell to $64,525M from $69,860M, shortening the cash conversion cycle to −56.8 days from −71.1. Part of the record is therefore a release of working capital that reverses as memory is pre-bought, not a permanent lift in earning power. The top line is not being smoothed either: deferred revenue of $14.9B is 3.2% of trailing revenue, and only $7,260M of nine-month revenue came out of the opening deferred balance. [S6]

### The balance sheet is not the risk; the asking price is

At 27 June 2026 cash and marketable securities were $146,517M against debt of $84,344M — net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M nine months earlier while $62,094M of stock was retired. The FY2025 notes carried $91.3B of principal with $12.4B payable within twelve months and $37.0B of future interest, commercial paper ran at a 4.19% weighted rate, leases add $16.8B of fixed obligations and purchase obligations $57.0B of manufacturing plus $29.3B of other commitments. Two items need a question rather than a red flag: $2,604M of unrealised losses on the securities book, and intangible assets that rose to $25,417M net from $13,301M — $38,220M gross, $12,803M accumulated amortisation — without the 10-Q disaggregating what was bought. [S5, S6]

| Return on equity | 171.9% | 157.4% | 171.4% | 148.8% | S5, S6 |
| Return on assets | 27.5% | 26.1% | 30.9% | 36.1% | S5, S6 |
| ROIC (equity + debt − cash basis; distorted) | 1,527% | 1,036% | 479% | 321% | S5, S6 |
| Free cash flow ÷ (equity + debt) | 57.5% | 66.5% | 57.3% | 71.2% | S5, S6 |
| Cash and marketable securities | 162,099 | 156,650 | 132,420 | 146,517 | S5, S6 |
| Net cash | 51,011 | 50,021 | 33,763 | 62,173 | S5, S6 |
| Days sales outstanding | 28.1 | 31.2 | 34.9 | 24.5 | S5, S6 |
| Days inventory outstanding | 10.8 | 12.6 | 9.4 | 16.9 | S5, S6 |
| Days payables outstanding | 106.7 | 119.7 | 115.4 | 98.3 | S5, S6 |

### Returns clear the cost of capital several times; the multiple does not clear the risk

ROE of 148.8% and ROA of 36.1% are genuine, and the reported ROIC of 320.6% is an artefact of $146.5B of cash and negative working capital that shrink invested capital to $45,347M. The measure that survives is cash return on book capital: free cash flow of $136,683M over equity plus debt of $191,864M, or 71.2%, against 57.3% in FY2025. With a ten-year Treasury at 4.93% and an equity risk premium of 4.5-5.5%, any plausible cost of equity of 9-11% is cleared several times; the constraint is the price, because a $5,072B market capitalisation on $128,930M of trailing net income is a 2.5% earnings yield. Capital allocation supports that reading rather than contradicting it: nine-month buybacks of $62,094M plus dividends of $11,778M are 67.0% of free cash flow, net cash rose, and shares fell 1.7% while net income rose 20.0%, so buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% EPS growth. This is not a debt-funded buyback story. [S6, S7]

### What the next print has to clear

No audited fiscal 2026 exists yet: Apple reports the September quarter on 2 November 2026, two days after this analysis, and the only forward numbers available are management's guidance of 9-11% revenue growth for that quarter ($111.7-113.7B off $102.5B) with iPhone growth in the mid-teens, against consensus of $56.4B of iPhone revenue for the quarter, $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4% on FY2025) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%). Sensitivity on trailing figures after a 17.3% tax rate: 200 basis points of gross margin is $0.52 of EPS (6.0%), 500 basis points is $1.31 (15.0%), losing the $20B search payment is $1.12 (12.9%) and a 10% fall in iPhone revenue at the 39.9% product margin is $0.55 (6.3%). Gross margin moves the outcome most because it applies to all $466,823M of revenue while a unit miss applies only to hardware. The limitation to state plainly: the FY2026 annual statements and the FY2026 10-K notes cannot be read before 2 November 2026, and the trailing figures mix a 52-week year with nine-month statements. [S71, S72]

### The margin is the record, and part of it was purchased

### Returns clear the cost of capital several times; the multiple does not clear the risk

No audited fiscal 2026 exists yet: Apple reports the September quarter on 2 November 2026, two days after this analysis, and the only forward numbers are management's guidance of 9-11% revenue growth for that quarter ($111.7-113.7B off $102.5B) with iPhone growth in the mid-teens, against consensus of $56.4B of iPhone revenue for the quarter, $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4% on FY2025) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%). The implication for an investor is that earnings quality is not the constraint on this name — the price is, since 39x trailing net income already assumes the 2026 margin is a base rather than a peak. The open diligence is specific: what gross margin does management guide for the December 2026 quarter, how much of FY2027 memory is contracted at fixed prices, and what was acquired for the $12,116M increase in net intangibles? [S71, S72]

Apple's profit is unusually cash-true. Over the twelve months to 27 June 2026 operating cash flow was $146,724M, capital expenditure $10,041M and free cash flow $136,683M against net income of $128,930M — a headline conversion of 1.06x, or 0.95-0.97x once a liability accrual is normalised, on capex of 2.2% of revenue, against 0.50x and 34.9% at Microsoft and 0.08x and 33.9% at Alphabet. The income statement behind that cash grew revenue from $383,285M in FY2023 to $416,161M in FY2025 and $466,823M trailing, with operating margin of 29.8%, 32.0% and 33.2%. The nine months to 27 June 2026 produced an incremental operating margin of 43.0% — $21,809M more operating income on $50,662M more revenue — which is the bull case in one line. The question is how much of that increment is repeatable. [S5, S6]

| $M unless stated | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M FY2026 | TTM | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 383,285 | 391,035 | 416,161 | 364,357 | 466,823 | S5, S6 |
| Gross profit | 169,148 | 180,683 | 195,201 | 178,782 | 227,123 | S5, S6 |
| Operating income | 114,301 | 123,216 | 133,050 | 122,432 | 154,859 | S5, S6 |
| Net income | 96,995 | 93,736 | 112,010 | 101,464 | 128,930 | S5, S6 |
| Diluted EPS ($) | 6.13 | 6.08 | 7.46 | 6.88 | 8.72 | S5, S6 |
| Diluted shares (M) | 15,813 | 15,408 | 15,005 | 14,750 | — | S5, S6 |
| Operating cash flow | 110,543 | 118,254 | 111,482 | 116,996 | 146,724 | S5, S6 |
| Capital expenditure | 10,959 | 9,447 | 12,715 | 6,799 | 10,041 | S5, S6 |
| Free cash flow | 99,584 | 108,807 | 98,767 | 110,197 | 136,683 | S5, S6 |
| Free cash flow ÷ net income | 1.03x | 1.16x | 0.88x | 1.09x | 1.06x | S5, S6 |
| Normalised free cash flow ÷ net income (est.) | — | — | — | — | 0.95-0.97x | S5, S6 |
| Buybacks plus dividends | 92,575 | 110,183 | 106,132 | 73,872 | 97,866 | S5, S6 |

| Comparison | Apple (TTM) | Microsoft (FY2026) | Alphabet (TTM) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free cash flow ÷ net income | 1.06x | 0.50x | 0.08x | S6, S49, S50 |
| Capital expenditure ÷ revenue | 2.2% | 34.9% | 33.9% | S6, S49, S50 |
| Gross margin | 48.7% | 67.9% | 59.7% (FY2025) | S6, S49, S50 |
| Operating margin | 33.2% | 46.8% | 33.3% | S6, S49, S15 |
| Ten-year Treasury yield, 30 October 2026 | 4.93% | — | — | S10 |

### The margin is the record, and part of it was purchased

Gross margin went from 44.1% in FY2023 to 46.2%, 46.9%, 49.1% in the nine months of FY2026 and 48.7% trailing, and the June 2026 quarter printed 50.1%, a record. Services, at a 76.3% gross margin, are 40.3% of the gross-profit pool on 25.8% of revenue; products are not. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9% on product mix and tariff refunds, and the 30 July 2026 release attributes 2 points of the quarter's gross margin and $0.11 of its $2.02 EPS to them. The cost side has turned: memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 against the 2025 average and the 10-Q expects the component trends "to intensify". A 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1%, is the level to capitalise. [S17, S68]

::: info warning
**Two percentage points of the record 50.1% gross margin are a one-off tariff refund, and the memory cycle is turning against the hardware line (S6, S17).**

The 30 July 2026 release puts the refund at 2 points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 quarterly EPS (S17); products gross margin of 39.9% compares with 36.9% a year earlier, while memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 and the 10-Q warns cost pressure will intensify (S6, S68). Two hundred basis points off the trailing gross margin is $0.52 of EPS, or 6.0% of the $8.72.
:::

### Cash conversion is real, but a liability accrual did the lifting

Nine-month operating cash flow rose $35,242M to $116,996M while net income rose $16,920M: non-cash add-backs added $1,956M more and working capital $16,366M more. The dominant line is other current and non-current liabilities, +$10,016M against -$15,161M a year earlier, a $25,177M swing concentrated in other non-current liabilities, up to $55,080M from $41,549M; without that line working capital was an $8,811M drag. The prior-year figure is distorted: the ~$15.8B Irish State Aid payment ran through the same line in the nine months to June 2025 (cash taxes paid of $37,332M against a $15,381M provision), and the $15,552M added to it in FY2024 is within $250M of the $15.8B payable; the clean swing is nearer $9.4B. Trailing free cash flow of $136,683M carries $14,101M from that line. Normalising it to zero, or to its $2.5B clean three-year average, gives $122.6-125.1B, conversion of 0.95-0.97x — still ahead of both peers — a 2.4-2.5% yield and 40.5-41.4x price to free cash flow. The $111.5B that subtracting the full $25.2B swing implies is too low because it treats a settlement-hit year as the baseline. The line is unexplained: a $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities against $13,270M of gross intangibles added and investing "other" of $1,780M points to deferred consideration, in which case that cash is an unpaid purchase, not earnings. Deferred revenue is no cushion either: 3.2% of trailing revenue, with only $7,260M of nine-month revenue out of the opening balance. [S5, S6]

### The balance sheet is not the risk; the asking price is

At 27 June 2026 cash and marketable securities were $146,517M against debt of $84,344M — net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M nine months earlier while $62,094M of stock was retired. FY2025 notes carried $91.3B of principal with $12.4B due within twelve months; leases add $16.8B of fixed obligations and purchase obligations $57.0B of manufacturing plus $29.3B of other commitments. Two items need a question: $2,604M of unrealised losses on the securities book, and intangibles up to $25,417M net from $13,301M, $12,116M in nine months, without the 10-Q saying what was bought. [S5, S6]

| Returns and working capital | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | TTM | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Return on equity | 171.9% | 157.4% | 171.4% | 148.8% | S5, S6 |
| Return on assets | 27.5% | 26.1% | 30.9% | 36.1% | S5, S6 |
| ROIC (equity + debt − cash basis; distorted) | 1,527% | 1,036% | 479% | 321% | S5, S6 |
| Free cash flow ÷ (equity + debt) | 57.5% | 66.5% | 57.3% | 71.2% | S5, S6 |
| Cash and marketable securities | 162,099 | 156,650 | 132,420 | 146,517 | S5, S6 |
| Net cash | 51,011 | 50,021 | 33,763 | 62,173 | S5, S6 |
| Days sales outstanding | 28.1 | 31.2 | 34.9 | 24.5 | S5, S6 |
| Days inventory outstanding | 10.8 | 12.6 | 9.4 | 16.9 | S5, S6 |
| Days payables outstanding | 106.7 | 119.7 | 115.4 | 98.3 | S5, S6 |
| Cash conversion cycle (days) | −67.8 | −75.8 | −71.1 | −56.8 | S5, S6 |
| Effective tax rate | 14.7% | 24.1% | 15.6% | 17.3% | S5, S6 |

### Returns clear the cost of capital several times; the multiple does not clear the risk

ROE of 148.8% and ROA of 36.1% are genuine, and the reported ROIC of 320.6% is an artefact of $146.5B of cash and negative working capital that shrink invested capital to $45,347M. The measure that survives is cash return on book capital: normalised free cash flow of about $125B over equity plus debt of $191,864M, or 65.2%, against 57.3% in FY2025. With the ten-year Treasury at 4.93% and an equity risk premium of 4.5-5.5%, a cost of equity of 9-11% is cleared several times; the constraint is the price: $5,072B of market capitalisation on $128,930M of trailing net income is a 2.5% earnings yield. Capital allocation agrees: nine-month buybacks of $62,094M plus dividends of $11,778M are 67.0% of free cash flow, net cash rose, and shares fell 1.7% while net income rose 20.0%, so buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% EPS growth. This is not a debt-funded buyback story. [S6, S7]

### What the next print has to clear

No audited fiscal 2026 exists: Apple reports the September quarter on 2 November 2026, and the only forward numbers are management's guidance of 9-11% revenue growth for that quarter ($111.7-113.7B off $102.5B) with iPhone growth in the mid-teens, against consensus of $56.4B for the quarter, $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4% on FY2025) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%). Sensitivity on trailing figures after a 17.3% tax rate: 200 basis points of gross margin is $0.52 of EPS (6.0%), 500 basis points is $1.31 (15.0%), losing the $20B search payment is $1.12 (12.9%) and a 10% fall in iPhone revenue at the 39.9% product margin is $0.55 (6.3%). Gross margin moves the outcome most because it applies to all $466,823M of revenue while a unit miss applies only to hardware. For the investor, earnings quality is not the constraint; the price is, since 39x trailing net income already assumes the 2026 margin is a base rather than a peak. The open diligence: what gross margin management guides for the December 2026 quarter, how much FY2027 memory is contracted at fixed prices, what was acquired for the $12,116M of net intangibles, and what sits in the $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities? [S71, S72]
